title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
山東鄉試錄序
國家用儒爲治其來尚矣學校
以養之者儒之學得正道也
科目以取之者儒之進得正
路也台揆庶尹胥此焉出儒
之識又得予名器之正也用
其重儒而不輕也蓋□□數
===
惟我
朝自
祖宗有天下傳歷百年用儒之效
一本之躬行
皇上嗣登大寶尤注意於用儒首
幸太學親謁孔子尊儒道也太
學生許就鄉試廣儒路也擢
punctuated:
山東鄉試錄序

國家用儒爲治，其來尚矣。學校以養之者，儒之學得正道也；科目以取之者，儒之進得正路也；台揆庶尹胥此焉出，儒之識又得予名器之正也。用其重儒而不輕也，蓋□□數。惟我朝自祖宗有天下，傳歷百年，用儒之效，一本之躬行。皇上嗣登大寶，尤注意於用儒：首幸太學，親謁孔子，尊儒道也；太學生許就鄉試，廣儒路也；擢
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shandong Provincial Examination

The employment of Confucian scholars by the state to achieve good governance goes back to remote antiquity. By nurturing them through schools, the learning of Confucian scholars attains the orthodox Way; by selecting them through the examination categories, the advancement of Confucian scholars attains the proper path; and as Grand Councilors and the various officials all emerge from this, the discernment of Confucian scholars also attains the proper bestowal of titles and ranks [?]. Because it values Confucian scholars and does not treat them lightly, indeed [… illegible …].

In our Dynasty, since our Imperial Ancestors came to possess the Empire, transmitted down through a hundred years, the efficacy of employing Confucian scholars has been rooted entirely in personal practice. Since His Majesty succeeded to the Great Throne, he has paid special attention to the employment of Confucian scholars: first visiting the Imperial University and personally paying homage to Confucius, which is to honor the Confucian Way; permitting Imperial University Students to sit for the Provincial Examination, which is to broaden the Confucian path; and promoting…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
官九載亦復聽其會試又所
以處儒之有遺才也曠古所
無之典
皇上毅然行之海内人心踴躍思
奮豈偶然而已哉成化紀元
之初適當大比山東藩臬重
臣恭循故事禮聘儒紳以司
===
文衡至期合六郡及邉徼文
學之士一千有竒而群試之
于時巡撫左副都御史賈銓
綱維經畫百度一新内而提
調則左布政使原傑左參政
葉冕監試則按察使李裕副
使莊歙外而防範賛襄則都
punctuated: 官九載，亦復聽其會試，又所以處儒之有遺才也。曠古所無之典，皇上毅然行之，海内人心踴躍思奮，豈偶然而已哉！成化紀元之初，適當大比，山東藩臬重臣恭循故事，禮聘儒紳，以司文衡。至期，合六郡及邉徼文學之士一千有竒而群試之。于時，巡撫左副都御史賈銓綱維經畫，百度一新；内而提調則左布政使原傑、左參政葉冕，監試則按察使李裕、副使莊歙；外而防範賛襄則都
translation_en: …appointed to office for nine years are also permitted to take the Metropolitan Examination, which is further a way of accommodating Confucian scholars whose talents might otherwise have been overlooked. Such ordinances, unprecedented since antiquity, have been resolutely carried out by His Majesty. That the hearts of people throughout the realm leap with eagerness to exert themselves is surely no mere accident! At the beginning of the first year of the Chenghua reign (1465), which coincided with the triennial examination cycle, the senior Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commission officials of Shandong reverently followed established precedent and with due ceremony invited Confucian gentry to take charge of weighing the literary compositions. When the appointed time arrived, they gathered more than one thousand men of learning from the six prefectures and the frontier marches and tested them together. At that time, the Grand Coordinator and Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Jia Quan 賈銓 directed and planned the overarching arrangements, renewing all regulations and procedures. Within the examination compound, serving as Proctors were the Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Yuan Jie 原傑 and Left Administration Vice Commissioner Ye Mian 葉冕, while serving as Monitoring Officials were the Surveillance Commissioner Li Yu 李裕 and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhuang Xi 莊歙; outside, taking precautions and assisting in the management were the…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
參政李讚陳雲鵬副使張秤
李琮左參議江玭右參議□□
恪僉事劉進莊昇徐㲄王黎
周濠茂彪而巡按監察御史
朱𥌒則嚴考較以杜倖進除
宿弊以靖文場寔臨涖而總
司之暨百執事與啓等亦皆
===
祗承
德意務求真儒之選迨撤棘得文
之中式者七十五人謹書成
錄將獻諸
上而傳之四方用昭賓興盛舉謂
宜有序猥及於啓竊惟儒道
與世道相關世道之泰儒道
punctuated:
參政李讚、陳雲鵬，副使張秤、李琮，左參議江玭，右參議□□恪，僉事劉進、莊昇、徐㲄、王黎、周濠、茂彪。而巡按監察御史朱𥌒，則嚴考較以杜倖進，除宿弊以靖文場，寔臨涖而總司之。暨百執事與啓等，亦皆祗承德意，務求真儒之選。迨撤棘，得文之中式者七十五人。謹書成錄，將獻諸上而傳之四方，用昭賓興盛舉。謂宜有序，猥及於啓。
竊惟儒道與世道相關。世道之泰，儒道
translation_en:
… Administration Vice Commissioners Li Zan 李讚 and Chen Yunpeng 陳雲鵬; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhang Cheng 張秤 and Li Cong 李琮; Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Jiang Pin 江玭; Right Assistant Administration Commissioner […]-ke □□恪; and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Liu Jin 劉進, Zhuang Sheng 莊昇, Xu Gu 徐㲄, Wang Li 王黎, Zhou Hao 周濠, and Mao Biao 茂彪. Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor Zhu Mian 朱𥌒 enforced strict evaluation to prevent opportunistic advancement and eradicated longstanding abuses to bring order to the examination compound, personally presiding over and directing the entire undertaking. Along with all the various functionaries, I, Qi 啓, and my colleagues likewise reverently upheld the Emperor's virtuous intent, striving to select true Confucian scholars. When the thorny barriers of the compound were removed at the conclusion of the examination, seventy-five men were found whose essays met the standard. Their names and essays have been carefully compiled into a record to be presented to His Majesty and circulated throughout the realm, thereby illustrating this grand occasion of selecting worthy guests for the court. Deeming that there ought to be a preface, they undeservedly turned to me, Qi.

I venture to reflect that the Way of the Confucians is bound up with the Way of the world. When the Way of the world flourishes in peace, it is because the Way of the Confucians…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
之行也肆唐虞三代世底雍
熈萬物得所有堯舜禹湯文
武以儒道君天下皐夔稷契
伊傅周召以儒道相天下當
時嘉謀善政載諸方册足以
垂法萬世有周之末先王之
教日以湮微於是天生孔子
===
===
刪述六經以儒道師天下譬
之規矩準繩必由是而後為
圓為方為平直也三代而下
享國長久者莫若漢唐宋其
間君臣相遇足以有為于一
時蓋亦彷彿乎儒道也我
皇上法

之行也肆唐虞三代世底雍
熙萬物得所有堯舜禹湯文
武以儒道君天下皐夔稷契
伊傅周召以儒道相天下當
時嘉謨善政載諸方冊足以
垂法萬世under
punctuated: 之行也。肆唐、虞、三代，世底雍熈，萬物得所，有堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武以儒道君天下，皐、夔、稷、契、伊、傅、周、召以儒道相天下。當時嘉謀善政載諸方册，足以垂法萬世。有周之末，先王之教日以湮微，於是天生孔子，刪述六經，以儒道師天下。譬之規矩準繩，必由是而後為圓、為方、為平直也。三代而下，享國長久者莫若漢、唐、宋，其間君臣相遇，足以有為于一時，蓋亦彷彿乎儒道也。我皇上法
translation_en: …is the practice [of the Confucian Way]. Thus, in the eras of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Three Dynasties, the world attained harmonious peace and all things found their proper place, for there were Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu ruling the empire as sovereigns through the Confucian Way, and Gao [Yao], Kui, Ji, Xie, Yi [Yin], Fu [Yue], the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao assisting the empire as ministers through the Confucian Way. The fine counsels and good governance of those times are recorded in the historical tablets, sufficient to hand down a model for ten thousand generations. At the end of the Zhou dynasty, the teachings of the former kings grew daily more obscure and faint; thereupon Heaven brought forth Confucius, who edited and transmitted the Six Classics, teaching the empire as a master through the Confucian Way. Likened to the compass, carpenter's square, level, and plumb line, it is only by following these that things can be made round, square, level, and straight. From the Three Dynasties onward, none enjoyed greater longevity of rule than the Han, Tang, and Song; during those periods, when sovereigns and ministers met in mutual accord and were able to accomplish great things in their own times, it was surely because they too approximated the Confucian Way. Our August Emperor emulates…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
祖宗而爲治一皆本諸堯舜禹湯
文武周公孔子之道以儒道
君天下莫盛於
今日諸君子作於
聖化皆負儒業由鄉舉而捷春闈
奉
廷對衣被寵光良有日矣尚思
===
聖天子崇儒之盛意毋俾唐虞三
代之豪傑專美于前斯不負
儒者之名矣若然匪直爲科
目之光實斯文之光
邦家之光也幸相與勉之
山西平陽府霍州儒學學正
punctuated:
祖宗而爲治，一皆本諸堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、周公、孔子之道，以儒道君天下，莫盛於今日。諸君子作於聖化，皆負儒業，由鄉舉而捷春闈，奉廷對，衣被寵光，良有日矣。尚思聖天子崇儒之盛意，毋俾唐、虞、三代之豪傑專美于前，斯不負儒者之名矣。若然，匪直爲科目之光，實斯文之光、邦家之光也。幸相與勉之。
山西平陽府霍州儒學學正
translation_en:
… [Our Emperor models himself on the] Ancestors in governing, basing everything entirely upon the Way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, King Wu, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius. Ruling all under Heaven by means of the Confucian Way has never been more flourishing than it is today. You gentlemen have arisen under His sagely transformation and all carry on the Confucian profession. Proceeding from the Provincial Examination to triumph in the spring Metropolitan Examination, presenting your replies at the Palace Examination, and being clothed in imperial favor and glory—truly that day is not far off! May you ever bear in mind the Sage Son of Heaven's grand intention in honoring Confucianism, and not let the outstanding heroes of the Tang, Yu, and Three Dynasties monopolize the glory before you; thus you will not fail to live up to the name of Confucians. If so, you will not merely be an honor to the examination system, but truly an honor to This Culture and an honor to the state. I hope that you will encourage one another in this.

Director of Studies of the Confucian School of Huo Department in Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, …

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
為仁由己而由人乎哉顏淵曰請問其目
子曰非禮勿視非禮勿聽非禮勿言
非禮勿動
不誠無物是故君子誠之為貴誠者非自
成己而已也所以成物也
詩云雨我公田遂及我私惟助為有公田
由此觀之雖周亦助也設為庠序學
校以教之庠者養也校者教也序者
射也夏曰校殷曰序周曰庠學則三
代共之皆所以明人倫也
===
易
六三觀我生進退未失
道也六四觀國之光利用賓于王象
曰觀國之光尚賓也
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「為仁由己，而由人乎哉？」顏淵曰：「請問其目。」子曰：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」

不誠無物。是故君子誠之為貴。誠者，非自成己而已也，所以成物也。

《詩》云：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」惟助為有公田。由此觀之，雖周亦助也。設為庠、序、學、校以教之。庠者，養也；校者，教也；序者，射也。夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠；學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。

易

六三，觀我生，進退。……未失道也。六四，觀國之光，利用賓于王。《象》曰：「觀國之光」，尚賓也。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

"The practice of humanity depends on oneself; does it depend on others?" Yan Yuan said, "I beg to ask for the specifics." The Master said, "Do not look at what is contrary to ritual; do not listen to what is contrary to ritual; do not speak what is contrary to ritual; do not make any movement that is contrary to ritual."

Without sincerity, there would be nothing. Therefore, the gentleman values the attainment of sincerity. Sincerity is not merely the completion of oneself; it is that by which one completes other things.

The Book of Odes says: "May it rain on our public fields, and then reach our private ones." Only under the mutual-aid (zhu) system are there public fields. Viewed from this, even the Zhou also used the mutual-aid system. Establish community schools—xiang, xu, xue, and xiao—to instruct them. Xiang means nourishing; xiao means teaching; xu means archery. The Xia called them xiao, the Yin called them xu, and the Zhou called them xiang; as for xue, the Three Dynasties shared the name in common. All of them are means to clarify human relationships.

Book of Changes

Six in the third place: Contemplating my own life, to advance or retreat. … [has] not lost the Way. Six in the fourth place: Contemplating the glory of the state, it is beneficial to be welcomed as a guest by the king. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "'Contemplating the glory of the state'—this esteems being a guest."

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
利有攸往中正有慶
歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後
掛乾之策二百一十有六坤之策百
四十有四凡三百有六十當期之日
理財正辭禁民爲非曰義
書
導沇水東流爲濟入于河溢爲滎東出于
陶丘北又東至于菏又東北會于汶
===
亦越文王武王克知三有宅心灼見三有
俊心以敬事上帝立民長伯立政任
人準夫牧作三事虎賁綴衣趣馬小
尹左右攜僕百司庶府大都小伯藝
人表臣百司太史尹伯庶常吉士
又北東入于海
政貴有恒辭尚體要不惟好異商俗靡靡
利口惟賢餘風未殄公其念哉
punctuated:
利有攸往，中正有慶。
歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。
理財正辭，禁民爲非曰義。
《書》
導沇水，東流爲濟，入于河，溢爲滎，東出于陶丘北，又東至于菏，又東北會于汶，又北東入于海。
亦越文王、武王，克知三有宅心，灼見三有俊心，以敬事上帝，立民長伯。立政：任人、準夫、牧，作三事；虎賁、綴衣、趣馬、小尹、左右攜僕、百司庶府；大都、小伯、藝人、表臣百司、太史、尹伯、庶常吉士。
政貴有恒，辭尚體要，不惟好異。商俗靡靡，利口惟賢，餘風未殄，公其念哉！
translation_en:
“‘It is favorable to have somewhere to go’: through centrality and correctness there is blessing.”
“One places the remainder between the fingers to represent the intercalary month. In five years there are two intercalations, and therefore one places the remainder between the fingers twice and afterward suspends a stalk. The stalks of Qian number two hundred and sixteen; the stalks of Kun number one hundred and forty-four. In all they are three hundred and sixty, corresponding to the days of a cycle of the year.”
“Ordering wealth, rectifying words, and forbidding the people from doing wrong is called righteousness.”
Book of Documents (Shu)
“He conducted the Yan River; flowing east it became the Ji, entered the Yellow River, overflowed to form the Xing Marsh, emerged eastward north of Taoqiu, went further east to the He Marsh, went further northeast to join the Wen River, and went further north and east to enter the sea.”
“And when it came to King Wen and King Wu, they were able to know the hearts of the three holders of office and clearly perceive the hearts of the three men of eminence, thereby reverently serving the Supreme Lord and establishing chiefs and leaders for the people. In establishing government: the Renren (appointees), Zhunfu (guardians of the laws), and Mu (pastors) served as the three ministers; the Huben (imperial bodyguards), Zhuiyi (keepers of the robes), Quma (equerries), Xiaoyin (minor directors), personal attendants and grooms of the left and right, and the hundred officials and various storehouse keepers; the chiefs of large cities and leaders of small ones, men of specialized skills, the hundred officials serving as external ministers, the Taishi (Grand Scribes), Yinbo (directors and chiefs), and the many constant and worthy gentlemen.”
“In governance, constancy is prized; in proclamations, substance and conciseness are valued; do not merely delight in novelty. The customs of Shang were extravagant and decadent, countingglibness of tongue alone as worthiness. The lingering habits are not yet eradicated—may the Duke bear this in mind!”

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
其刑其罰其審克之
詩
孑孑干旄在浚之郊素絲紕之良馬四之
彼姝者子何以畀之孑孑干旟在浚
之都素絲組之良馬五之彼姝者子
何以予之孑孑干旌在浚之城素絲
祝之良馬六之彼姝者子何以告之
天立厥配受命既固
===
蓺之荏菽荏菽旆旆禾役穟穟麻麥幪幪
瓜瓞唪唪誕后稷之穡有相之道茀
厥豐草種之黃茂
率履不越遂視既發相土烈烈海外有截
帝命不違至于湯齊湯降不遲
春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕滕子來朝〔桓公二年〕荆人來聘
莊公二十三年公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭
punctuated:
其刑其罰，其審克之。

《詩》
孑孑干旄，在浚之郊。素絲紕之，良馬四之。彼姝者子，何以畀之？孑孑干旟，在浚之都。素絲組之，良馬五之。彼姝者子，何以予之？孑孑干旌，在浚之城。素絲祝之，良馬六之。彼姝者子，何以告之？
天立厥配，受命既固。
蓺之荏菽，荏菽旆旆，禾役穟穟，麻麥幪幪，瓜瓞唪唪。誕后稷之穡，有相之道。茀厥豐草，種之黃茂。
率履不越，遂視既發。相土烈烈，海外有截。帝命不違，至于湯齊。湯降不遲。

《春秋》
春，王正月〔隱公元年〕。滕子來朝〔桓公二年〕。荆人來聘，莊公二十三年。公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭
translation_en:
“In your punishments and your fines, examine them carefully and master them.”

Book of Odes (Shi):
“Conspicuous are the ox-tail standards, in the suburbs of Jun. With white silk threads they are bound; with teams of four fine horses. That admirable gentleman—what shall I give him? Conspicuous are the falcon banners, in the outlying towns of Jun. With white silk cords they are braided; with teams of five fine horses. That admirable gentleman—what shall I present to him? Conspicuous are the feathered standards, at the city wall of Jun. With white silk bands they are tied; with teams of six fine horses. That admirable gentleman—what shall I tell him?”
“Heaven established Its consort, and the Mandate he received became secure.”
“He planted large beans; the large beans grew luxuriantly. The rows of grain nodded ripely; the hemp and wheat grew dense and thick; the gourds and melons clustered abundantly. Truly, the husbandry of Hou Ji followed the way of assisting nature. Having cleared away the thick grass, he sowed the yellow and flourishing grains.”
“He followed the path without transgressing; when examined, his conduct proved fully manifest. Xiangtu was glorious and martial, and beyond the seas all was brought to order. The Mandate of the Supreme Ancestor did not depart, until in Tang it came to perfection. Tang was born not too late.”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
“Spring, the King’s first month [First year of Duke Yin].” “The Viscount of Teng came to court [Second year of Duke Huan].” “An envoy from Jing came on a mission of friendly inquiries, [Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang].” “The Duke met with the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng…”

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
伯衛子莒子盟于踐土　公朝于王所
僖公二十八年　天王使宰周公來聘〔僖公三十年〕
年
天子突救衛〔莊公六年〕　公會王人齊侯宋公衛侯
許男曹伯陳世子款盟于洮〔僖公八年〕　會王
人晉人宋人齊人陳人蔡人秦人盟于翟泉
僖公二十九年
宋公齊侯盟于□〔莊公三十二年〕　齊侯宋公江人
===
黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕　齊侯宋公江人黃人會
于陽穀〔僖公三年〕　□伐楚　楚屈完來盟
于師　盟于召陵　齊人執陳轅濤塗
及江人黃人伐陳　公孫茲帥師會齊人宋
人衛人鄭人許人曹人侵陳〔僖公四年〕　公及
齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯會
王世子于首止　諸侯盟于首止　鄭伯逃
歸不盟　楚人滅弦〔僖公五年〕　楚人圍許
punctuated:
伯、衛子、莒子盟于踐土，公朝于王所。僖公二十八年。天王使宰周公來聘〔僖公三十年〕。年。
天子突救衛〔莊公六年〕。公會王人、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、許男、曹伯、陳世子款盟于洮〔僖公八年〕。會王人、晉人、宋人、齊人、陳人、蔡人、秦人盟于翟泉。僖公二十九年。
宋公、齊侯盟于□〔莊公三十二年〕。齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕。齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕。□伐楚，楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。齊人執陳轅濤塗，及江人、黃人伐陳。公孫茲帥師會齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭人、許人、曹人侵陳〔僖公四年〕。公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會王世子于首止，諸侯盟于首止，鄭伯逃歸不盟。楚人滅弦〔僖公五年〕。楚人圍許…
translation_en:
… the Earl [of Zheng], the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju made a covenant at Jiantu; the Duke had an audience at the King's temporary residence (28th year of Duke Xi). The Heavenly King sent the Grand宰 [Prime Minister] Duke of Zhou to come on a mission of friendly inquiry [30th year of Duke Xi] [?].
Wangzi Tu [transcribed as "Tianzi Tu" (?)] relieved Wei [6th year of Duke Zhuang]. The Duke met an officer of the King, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Kuan, the Heir Apparent of Chen, and made a covenant at Tao [8th year of Duke Xi]. [He] met an officer of the King, a representative of Jin, a representative of Song, a representative of Qi, a representative of Chen, a representative of Cai, and a representative of Qin, and made a covenant at Diquan (29th year of Duke Xi).
The Duke of Song and the Marquis of Qi made a covenant at [Liangqiu (?)] [32nd year of Duke Zhuang]. The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, a representative of Jiang, and a representative of Huang made a covenant at Guan [2nd year of Duke Xi]. The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, a representative of Jiang, and a representative of Huang met at Yanggu [3rd year of Duke Xi]. [… (?)] attacked Chu; Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army, and made a covenant at Shaoling. The people of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen, and together with the people of Jiang and the people of Huang attacked Chen. Gongsun Zi led a force to join the people of Qi, the people of Song, the people of Wei, the people of Zheng, the people of Xu, and the people of Cao in invading Chen [4th year of Duke Xi]. The Duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the Royal Heir Apparent at Shouzhi; the feudal lords made a covenant at Shouzhi; the Earl of Zheng fled home and did not join the covenant. The people of Chu extinguished Xian [5th year of Duke Xi]. The people of Chu besieged Xu…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
僖公六年
季孫行父臧孫許叔孫僑如公孫嬰齊帥師會晉
郤克衛孫良夫曹公子首及齊侯戰于鞌
成公二年季孫宿叔老會晉士匄齊人宋人
衛人鄭公孫蠆曹人莒人邾人滕人薛人杞人小

===
禮記
制三公一命卷若有加則賜也不過九命
射之以樂也何以聽何以射
閏月則闔門左扉立于其中皮弁以日視朝
遂以食日中而餕奏而食日少牢朔月大
牢五飲上水漿酒醴酏
然則先王之爲樂也以法治也善則行象德
矣
第貳場
論
punctuated:
僖公六年。
季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師會晉郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌。成公二年。
季孫宿、叔老會晉士匄、齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭公孫蠆、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人會吳于向。襄公十四年。

《禮記》：
「制：三公一命卷，若有加，則賜也，不過九命。」
「射之以樂也，何以聽？何以射？」
「閏月，則闔門左扉，立于其中。皮弁以日視朝，遂以食。日中而餕，奏而食。日少牢，朔月大牢。五飲：上水、漿、酒、醴、酏。」
「然則先王之爲樂也，以法治也，善則行象德矣。」

Jisun Su 季孫宿 and Shu Lao 叔老 joined Shi Gai 士匄 of Jin 晉, the men of Qi 齊, the men of Song 宋, the men of Wei 衛, Gongsun Chai 公孫蠆 of Zheng 鄭, the men of Cao 曹, the men of Ju 莒, the men of Zhu 邾, the men of Teng 滕, the men of Xue 薛, the men of Qi 杞, and the men of Little Zhu 小邾 to meet with Wu 吳 at Xiang 向 [14th year of Duke Xiang 襄公].

Record of Rites (Liji 禮記):
"According to the regulations: the Three Dukes (Sangong 三公), if advanced one grade of appointment, wear the dragon robe; if there is any further addition, it is by special bestowal, not exceeding nine grades of appointment."
"In archery, one shoots in time with the music; how can one both listen to the music and shoot accurately?"
"In an intercalary month, he closes the left leaf of the gate and stands in the middle of the doorway. Wearing the white deerskin cap, he holds court daily, and thereupon takes his meal. At midday he eats the remains of the morning meal, with music playing as he eats. Daily the offering is a lesser sacrifice of a sheep and a pig (shaolao 少牢); on the first day of the month it is a great sacrifice of an ox, a sheep, and a pig (tailao 大牢). For the five drinks, water is placed highest, followed by sour rice-water, wine, sweet wine, and gruel."
"Therefore, when the former kings instituted music, they used it as a model for governance; when it is good, then conduct comes to resemble virtue."

Question: Since antiquity, emperors and kings have been reverent and cautious regarding penal law. This is because the law is the life of the people, and punishment is the frame [?] of the state; if one fails to weigh and deliberate upon them properly, the people will hardly know where to place…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
手足矣恭惟我
太祖高皇帝
御極之初即
命詳定律法
太宗文皇帝繼體守成亦許究抑自際
宣宗章皇帝又製五倫書頒行天下而於君道
篇悉載古今慎刑之意以昭鑒戒
聖德好生何其至歟然恤刑之條始之以何人
===
之言終之以何人之說下車泣囚其與
刑期于無刑之心同與異與納隍致麑
其與好生之德協與否與刑罰不中則
民無所措手足者其言何三見與死者
不可復生其語何四出與今
皇上明德慎罰屢詔恤刑固將與
祖宗同一盛心矣諸士子佩服
聖訓蓋亦有年他日倘為掌刑之官必將有以
punctuated: 手足矣。恭惟我太祖高皇帝御極之初，即命詳定律法；太宗文皇帝繼體守成，亦許究抑自際；宣宗章皇帝又製《五倫書》頒行天下，而於〈君道〉篇悉載古今慎刑之意，以昭鑒戒。聖德好生，何其至歟！然〈恤刑〉之條，始之以何人之言，終之以何人之說？「下車泣囚」，其與「刑期于無刑」之心同與異與？「納隍」、「致麑」，其與「好生之德」協與否與？「刑罰不中，則民無所措手足」者，其言何三見與？「死者不可復生」，其語何四出與？今皇上明德慎罰，屢詔恤刑，固將與祖宗同一盛心矣。諸士子佩服聖訓，蓋亦有年，他日倘為掌刑之官，必將有以
translation_en: … Now, respectfully considering our Grand Progenitor the Exalted Emperor (Taizu): at the beginning of his reign, he immediately ordered the detailed formulation of the penal laws. The Grand Ancestor the Cultured Emperor (Taizong), succeeding to the throne and preserving the accomplishments of his predecessor, also permitted those suffering from unredressed grievances to appeal directly [? 自際, for 自陳]. The Proclaiming Ancestor the Brilliant Emperor (Xuanzong) further compiled the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) and promulgated it throughout the empire; in the chapter on "The Way of the Ruler" (Jundao), he recorded in full the principles of prudence in punishment from antiquity to the present to serve as a clear mirror and warning. How supreme is the sacred virtue that loves life! Yet in the section on "Compassion in Punishments" (Xuxing), with whose words does it begin, and with whose discourse does it conclude? Is the mind that "stepped down from the carriage to weep for the prisoners" the same as or different from the mind that "uses punishments in the hope of ending punishments"? Do "feeling as if pushing people into a ditch" (nahuang) and "releasing the fawn" (zhini) accord or not accord with the "virtue that loves life"? Why does the saying "when punishments and penalties miss the mark, the people have nowhere to put hand or foot" appear three times? Why does the phrase "the dead cannot be brought back to life" occur in four places? Now His Majesty the Emperor illustrates virtue and is prudent in penalties, repeatedly issuing edicts calling for compassion in punishments; truly he shares the same magnificent heart as our Imperial Ancestors. You scholars have cherished and taken to heart the sacred instructions for some years now; if one day you should become officials in charge of punishments, you will surely have a way to…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
處之者願著于篇
問大學中庸聖賢傳授心法之書其言雖
博而誠敬二者足以該之夫敬爲大學
之要領何至傳三章始言緝熙敬止來
知此章之前亦有敬可言歟誠爲中庸
之樞紐何至十六章始言誠不可揜夫
知此章之前亦有誠可指歟敬之釋先
儒有言主一無適者有言整齊嚴肅者
===
有言常惺惺法者又有言收斂不容一
物者四言之中奚爲至切識之釋先儒
有以不欺爲言者有以不息爲言者有
以無妄爲言者又有以真實無妄爲言
者四語之中奚爲至要夫誠敬既爲庸
學之要學者欲從事於誠敬果當交致
其功歟抑或有先後緩急歟誠敬之說
亦未知始於何經歟願詳著之以觀居
punctuated:
處之者，願著于篇。
問：《大學》、《中庸》，聖賢傳授心法之書，其言雖博，而誠、敬二者足以該之。夫敬爲《大學》之要領，何至傳三章始言「緝熙敬止」？來知此章之前亦有敬可言歟？誠爲《中庸》之樞紐，何至十六章始言「誠不可揜」？夫知此章之前亦有誠可指歟？敬之釋，先儒有言「主一無適」者，有言「整齊嚴肅」者，有言「常惺惺法」者，又有言「收斂不容一物」者，四言之中奚爲至切？識之釋，先儒有以「不欺」爲言者，有以「不息」爲言者，有以「無妄」爲言者，又有以「真實無妄」爲言者，四語之中奚爲至要？夫誠、敬既爲《庸》、《學》之要，學者欲從事於誠、敬，果當交致其功歟？抑或有先後緩急歟？誠、敬之說，亦未知始於何經歟？願詳著之，以觀居
translation_en:
… handle these matters. Please set them forth in your essays.

Question: The Great Learning (Daxue) and the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) are books through which the sages and worthies transmitted the method of the mind (xinfa). Although their words are extensive, the two concepts of sincerity (cheng) and reverence (jing) suffice to encompass them. Now, reverence is the essential principle of the Great Learning; why is it not until the third chapter of the commentary that it first speaks of "continuing in bright reverence and resting in it"? I do not [?; 來 for 未] know whether before this chapter there is also anything that can be spoken of as reverence? Sincerity is the pivot of the Doctrine of the Mean; why is it not until the sixteenth chapter that it first says "sincerity cannot be concealed"? I do not [?; 夫 for 未] know whether before this chapter there is also anything that can be pointed to as sincerity? Regarding the explanation of reverence, among former Confucians there was one who spoke of "concentrating on one thing without departing from it," one who spoke of "orderliness and solemnity," one who spoke of "the method of remaining constantly alert," and also one who spoke of "gathering in the mind and not allowing a single thing in." Among these four statements, which is the most pertinent? Regarding the explanation of sincerity [?; 識 for 誠], among former Confucians there was one who spoke of it in terms of "no self-deception," one who spoke of it in terms of "unceasingness," one who spoke of it in terms of "freedom from falsity," and also one who spoke of it in terms of "genuineness and freedom from falsity." Among these four phrases, which is the most essential? Now, since sincerity and reverence are the essentials of the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning, when scholars wish to devote themselves to sincerity and reverence, ought they indeed to apply their efforts to both mutually, or is there an order of priority and urgency between them? Furthermore, it is not known in which classic the doctrines of sincerity and reverence originated. Please set this forth in detail, so that we may observe your…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
敬立誠之學
問明經進士兩科自隋唐以來而始盛論
者謂唐重明經而輕進士宋重進士而
輕明經何以知其然歟唐有欲罷明經
進士之科者其所以欲罷之意可得而
言歟其試之之法有以詩賦論策而復
加以經義之制者則自何時而立有臨
軒試以詩賦而復定以策試之制者則
===
自何時而始且糊名易書之制既立而
諸州之糊名易書則始於何時而易書
則又從何人請歟如傳義匿服之有禁
冒貢挾書之有條抑因何事而舉歟封
印卷首嚴禁秉燭又因何人之言而行
歟若受知先朝擢自下第偉有儀狀擢
居首選者可知其人歟又若懷州發解
素已銓次大名舉子自相推先者其人
punctuated:
敬立誠之學。
問：明經、進士兩科，自隋、唐以來而始盛。論者謂唐重明經而輕進士，宋重進士而輕明經，何以知其然歟？唐有欲罷明經、進士之科者，其所以欲罷之意可得而言歟？其試之之法，有以詩、賦、論、策而復加以經義之制者，則自何時而立？有臨軒試以詩、賦而復定以策試之制者，則自何時而始？且糊名、易書之制既立，而諸州之糊名、易書則始於何時？而易書則又從何人請歟？如傳義、匿服之有禁，冒貢、挾書之有條，抑因何事而舉歟？封印卷首、嚴禁秉燭，又因何人之言而行歟？若受知先朝、擢自下第，偉有儀狀、擢居首選者，可知其人歟？又若懷州發解、素已銓次，大名舉子、自相推先者，其人
translation_en:
… learning in abiding in reverence and establishing sincerity.

Question: The two examination categories of Classicist (mingjing) and Metropolitan Graduate (jinshi) first flourished from the Sui and Tang dynasties onward. Commentators say that the Tang valued the Classicist degree and slighted the Metropolitan Graduate degree, whereas the Song valued the Metropolitan Graduate degree and slighted the Classicist degree; how do we know this to be so? In the Tang there were those who wished to abolish the Classicist and Metropolitan Graduate categories; can the reasons why they wished to abolish them be stated? As for the methods of examining them, when was the system established that tested with poetry (shi), rhapsodies (fu), discourses (lun), and policy questions (ce), and then further added expositions on the Classics (jingyi)? When did the system begin in which the emperor personally presided at the palace to test candidates with poetry and rhapsodies, and then settled on testing them with policy questions? Moreover, once the regulations for sealing names (huming) and transcribing examination papers (yishu) were established, when did sealing names and transcribing papers in the various prefectures begin, and at whose request was the transcription of papers instituted? Furthermore, because of what incidents were the prohibitions against passing along model expositions and concealing mourning obligations, or the articles against fraudulent tribute status and smuggling texts into the examination hall, enacted? And on account of whose words were the sealing and stamping of the front of examination rolls and the strict prohibition against holding candles put into practice? As for the one who had won recognition under a previous reign and was promoted despite failing the examination, and the one of imposing appearance and bearing who was elevated to first place—can who those men were be known? And as for the candidates dispatched from Huaizhou who had already been ranked in advance, and the candidates of Daming who yielded precedence among themselves—who those men…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
亦可考歟諸士子於科目必嘗究其實
矣請悉以對
問理學類編一書皆集先儒之格言而示
學者以窮理之要也姑舉其槩以質之
夫編集是書固有次第而其目可歷陳
歟講論太極固非一人而精微孰為得
歟天地有闔闢驗之於何物天一而生
水徵之於何事陽唱陰和則雨亦有西
===
風而雨者何地歟陰陽氣和乃雨亦有
龍能致之者何義歟雷本氣也或擊人
與物而成斧石者果神物所主歟電亦
氣也或閃爍激疾如金蛇飛騰之狀者
何形氣若是歟論陰陽則有以象類言
有以動靜言有以對待言又有以錯綜
言者何不同歟論五行則有以質而語
其生之序有以氣而語其行之序有統
punctuated:
亦可考歟？諸士子於科目，必嘗究其實矣，請悉以對。
問：《理學類編》一書，皆集先儒之格言，而示學者以窮理之要也。姑舉其槩以質之。夫編集是書，固有次第，而其目可歷陳歟？講論太極，固非一人，而精微孰為得歟？天地有闔闢，驗之於何物？天一而生水，徵之於何事？陽唱陰和則雨，亦有西風而雨者，何地歟？陰陽氣和乃雨，亦有龍能致之者，何義歟？雷本氣也，或擊人與物而成斧石者，果神物所主歟？電亦氣也，或閃爍激疾如金蛇飛騰之狀者，何形氣若是歟？論陰陽，則有以象類言，有以動靜言，有以對待言，又有以錯綜言者，何不同歟？論五行，則有以質而語其生之序，有以氣而語其行之序，有統
translation_en:
…also be verified? You gentlemen have surely investigated the historical facts regarding the examination system; please respond in full.

Question: The book Classified Compendium of the Learning of Principle (Lixue leibian 理學類編) compiles the maxims of former Confucians to show scholars the essentials of fathoming principle. Let us raise its main points to inquire into them. The compilation of this book certainly follows a sequence; can its headings be enumerated in turn? More than one person has expounded upon the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji 太極); who has grasped its subtlest essentials? Heaven and Earth have their closing and opening; by what things is this verified? "Heaven is One and generates Water"; by what affairs is this evidenced? When yang leads and yin harmonizes, rain falls, yet there are also places where rain comes with a west wind—what lands are these? It is when the qi of yin and yang are in harmony that rain falls, yet dragons are also able to bring it about—what is the meaning of this? Thunder is fundamentally qi, yet sometimes it strikes people or things and forms axe-shaped stones—is this truly governed by a divine creature? Lightning is also qi, yet sometimes it flashes and darts rapidly in the shape of a soaring golden serpent—how do form and qi come to be like this? In discussing yin and yang, some speak in terms of emblematic categories, some in terms of movement and stillness, some in terms of opposition and complementarity, and others in terms of interweaving and alternation—why do they differ? In discussing the Five Phases (wuxing 五行), some speak of the sequence of their generation in terms of material substance, some speak of the sequence of their operation in terms of qi, some address them as a unified…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
而言之者又有錯而言之者何相異歟
願著于篇以觀窮理之學
問
國家承平之時亦不可忘武備也武備脩則
教閱有方講習有素萬一不虞用之以
禦侮銷患無難事矣稽之成周四時講
武所謂振旅茇舍治兵大閱是已其制
可得而詳歟秦不師古盡去成周之法
===
之興內則有東之之制外則有都試之
名李唐之世府兵有一時之講顯德有
習射之較并州城北驟山之下又有
有講焉至于有宋四時有講武之儀
郊行大閱之禮朱明之池講武之儀
相繼有習焉可各指其實而陳之歟抑
有優劣之可議歟其亦有合於成周之
制否歟惟□□哉
punctuated:
而言之者，又有錯而言之者，何相異歟？願著于篇，以觀窮理之學。

問：國家承平之時，亦不可忘武備也。武備脩，則教閱有方，講習有素，萬一不虞，用之以禦侮銷患，無難事矣。稽之成周，四時講武，所謂振旅、茇舍、治兵、大閱是已，其制可得而詳歟？秦不師古，盡去成周之法；之興，內則有東之之制，外則有都試之名。李唐之世，府兵有一時之講，顯德有習射之較，并州城北、驟山之下，又有有講焉。至于有宋，四時有講武之儀，郊行大閱之禮，朱明之池、講武之儀，相繼有習焉。可各指其實而陳之歟？抑有優劣之可議歟？其亦有合於成周之制否歟？惟□□哉…
translation_en:
…and those who speak of them comprehensively, and others who speak of them in alternation—why do they differ from one another? I wish you to set this forth in your essay, so that we may observe your learning in the exhaustive investigation of principle.

Question: Even in times of dynastic peace, the state must not forget military preparedness. When military preparedness is cultivated, training and reviews have a proper method, and drills and exercises are habitually practiced; should an unexpected crisis arise, employing them to repel external aggression and eliminate disaster will be a matter of no difficulty. Examining the era of Completed Zhou (Cheng Zhou), military exercises were conducted in the four seasons: these were what are called the Spring Drill (zhenlü), the Summer Drill (bashe), the Autumn Drill (zhibing), and the Great Winter Review (dayue). Can their institutional details be recounted in full?

Qin did not model itself on antiquity and completely discarded the institutions of Completed Zhou. With the rise of [Han] [?], in the capital there was the institution of the Eastern [Review?] [?], and in the provinces there was the designation of the Autumn Military Competition (dushi). In the era of the Li-surname Tang dynasty, the garrison militia (fubing) had seasonal exercises, in the Xiande Hall there were archery competitions, and north of Bingzhou city and at the foot of Li Mountain [?] there were also reviews and exercises [?]. Coming down to the Song dynasty, there were ceremonies for military exercises in the four seasons, the ritual of the Great Review was performed in the suburbs, and at the Zhuming Pool and the [Hall for] Ceremonies of Military Exercises [?], drills were conducted in succession. Can you point out the facts of each and set them forth? Or can their relative merits and defects be discussed? And did they accord or not with the institutions of Completed Zhou? Truly, Our [Imperial Dynasty] [?]…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
朝重熙累洽有安不忘危之□□□□□□
武有方盖已逺過漢唐宋□□□□□
休矣孔子曰有文事者必有□□□□□
子素有志於文武者也其爲我□□
punctuated: 朝重熙累洽，有安不忘危之□□□□□□武有方，盖已逺過漢、唐、宋□□□□□休矣。孔子曰：「有文事者必有□□。」□□□子素有志於文武者也，其爲我□□。
translation_en: …Dynasty, with successive reigns of luminous peace and pervasive harmony, has [the foresight of?] not forgetting danger in times of security, and [its training in?] military affairs is well-regulated; indeed, it has already far surpassed the Han, Tang, and Song […] in splendor! Confucius said: “Whoever has civil responsibilities must also have [military preparations].” [You, gentlemen,] have long set your minds upon both civil and military affairs; [set this forth] for me […].

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
四書
爲仁由己而由人乎哉顏淵曰請問其目子曰
非禮勿視非禮勿聽非禮勿言非禮勿動
王綸
同考試官訓導羅　批此題本平易場中作者冗繁惟此
考試官學正吳　批此篇詞理通暢足見講學
考試官教諭梁　批理有定見辭不蹈襲宜置優選
作簡當可采
聖人告大賢爲仁當决其機於己答大賢問目當制
===
其欲於己盡爲仁由己用力之機要也非禮勿視聽
言動用力之條目也欲收克復之功豈外是哉昔聖
人因顏子問仁而告之及此若曰爲仁之道固在於
克己復禮而欲克己復禮果何所用力耶是故仁者
本心之全德非由外鑠我也今焉克己以爲仁則克
己之功我所當任他人庸得而預之仁者吾心之天
理非有待於外也今焉復禮以爲仁則復禮之力己
所當盡若人奚得而干之此其機之在我而無難也
顏子一聞其言則於天理人欲之際已判然矣故不
punctuated:
四書
「爲仁由己，而由人乎哉？」顏淵曰：「請問其目。」子曰：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」
王綸
同考試官訓導羅批：此題本平易，場中作者冗繁，惟此作簡當，可采。
考試官學正吳批：此篇詞理通暢，足見講學。
考試官教諭梁批：理有定見，辭不蹈襲，宜置優選。
聖人告大賢爲仁當决其機於己，答大賢問目當制其欲於己。盡「爲仁由己」，用力之機要也；「非禮勿視、聽、言、動」，用力之條目也。欲收克復之功，豈外是哉？昔聖人因顏子問仁而告之及此，若曰：爲仁之道，固在於克己復禮；而欲克己復禮，果何所用力耶？是故仁者，本心之全德，非由外鑠我也。今焉克己以爲仁，則克己之功，我所當任，他人庸得而預之？仁者，吾心之天理，非有待於外也。今焉復禮以爲仁，則復禮之力，己所當盡，若人奚得而干之？此其機之在我而無難也。顏子一聞其言，則於天理人欲之際已判然矣，故不
translation_en:
Four Books

"The practice of humanity depends on oneself; does it depend on others?" Yan Yuan [顏淵] said, "I beg to ask for the specific items." The Master said, "Do not look at what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not listen to what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not speak what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not make any movement that is contrary to ritual propriety."

Wang Lun [王綸]

Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Luo, comments: This topic is inherently plain and accessible, yet the writers in the examination hall produced verbose and convoluted essays; only this composition is concise and fitting, worthy of selection.
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wu, comments: Both the diction and the reasoning of this essay flow smoothly, amply demonstrating genuine scholarly study.
Examiner, County Director of Studies Liang, comments: The reasoning shows settled insight, and the phrasing does not merely copy predecessors; it ought to be placed in the superior grade.

The Sage instructed the Great Worthy that in practicing humanity one must determine the decisive pivot within oneself, and in answering the Great Worthy's inquiry about the specific items, taught that one must restrain desires within oneself. Truly [尽 for 蓋?], "the practice of humanity depends on oneself" is the pivotal essential for exerting effort; "do not look, listen, speak, or move contrary to ritual propriety" are the specific items for exerting effort. If one wishes to reap the achievement of overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety, how could it lie outside of this?

In the past, because Master Yan asked about humanity, the Sage instructed him up to this point, as if to say: The way of practicing humanity assuredly lies in overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety; yet if one wishes to overcome the self and return to ritual propriety, where indeed should one exert effort? Therefore, humanity is the complete virtue of the original mind, not something fused onto me from the outside. Now, in overcoming the self so as to practice humanity, the work of overcoming the self is a responsibility I myself must bear—how could others possibly take part in it? Humanity is the Heavenly Principle within my own mind, not something dependent on the outside. Now, in returning to ritual propriety so as to practice humanity, the effort of returning to ritual propriety is something I myself must exhaust—how could other men possibly interfere with it? This is why the decisive pivot lies within oneself and presents no difficulty.

Once Master Yan heard these words, the boundary between Heavenly Principle and human desire was already crystal clear to him; therefore he did not…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
復有所疑問而直請其條目焉聖人復告之曰目司
視而耳司聽也視聽非禮則有以害吾仁矣故非禮
之聲色必禁止之而弗視弗聽焉此防其自外入而
動於內者爲何如口主言而身主動也言動非禮則
有以壞吾仁矣故非禮之念慮必消弭之而不言不
動焉此謹其自內出而接於外者又何如內外交進
克復之功盡矣仁之爲道孰有加於此哉抑此章問
答乃聖門傳授心法切要之言也非顏子之明則雖
有克己復禮天下歸仁之告必不能察其幾非顏子
===
至健則雖有爲仁由己與夫四勿之說必不能致其
決此夫子所以獨告顏子有以夫
不誠無物是故君子誠之爲貴誠者非自成己
而已也所以成物也
同考試官教諭徐　批中庸一篇本於性理場中作者多泛
而不切惟此篇詞理俱到可取
李瑾
考試官教諭桊　批理明文暢優於衆作
考試官學正吳　批此篇得子思語誠之旨而詞又
punctuated:
復有所疑問，而直請其條目焉。聖人復告之曰：「目司視而耳司聽也。視聽非禮，則有以害吾仁矣。故非禮之聲色，必禁止之，而弗視弗聽焉。此防其自外入而動於內者，爲何如？口主言而身主動也。言動非禮，則有以壞吾仁矣。故非禮之念慮，必消弭之，而不言不動焉。此謹其自內出而接於外者，又何如？」內外交進，克復之功盡矣。仁之爲道，孰有加於此哉！抑此章問答，乃聖門傳授心法切要之言也。非顏子之明，則雖有「克己復禮，天下歸仁」之告，必不能察其幾；非顏子至健，則雖有「爲仁由己」與夫「四勿」之說，必不能致其決。此夫子所以獨告顏子，有以夫！
不誠無物。是故君子誠之爲貴。誠者，非自成己而已也，所以成物也。
李瑾
同考試官教諭徐　批：《中庸》一篇本於性理，場中作者多泛而不切，惟此篇詞理俱到，可取。
考試官教諭桊　批：理明文暢，優於衆作。
考試官學正吳　批：此篇得子思語誠之旨，而詞又
translation_en:
… did not have any further doubts to ask about, and instead asked directly for the specific items of practice. The Sage again instructed him, saying in effect: "The eyes are in charge of seeing and the ears are in charge of hearing. If seeing and hearing are contrary to ritual propriety, they will harm one's benevolence. Therefore, sights and sounds that are contrary to ritual propriety must be prohibited, so that one neither looks at nor listens to them. How thorough this is in guarding against what enters from the outside and stirs the inside! The mouth governs speech and the body governs action. If speech and action are contrary to ritual propriety, they will ruin one's benevolence. Therefore, thoughts and intentions that are contrary to ritual propriety must be dispelled, so that one neither speaks nor acts upon them. And how careful this is in watching over what issues from the inside and engages with the outside!" When inner and outer cultivation advance together, the work of overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety is complete. As for the Way of benevolence, what could surpass this? Moveover, the questions and answers in this chapter are the essential words by which the school of the Sage transmitted the method of the mind. Without the clarity of Master Yan (Yan Hui 顏回), even when given the teaching of "overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety, whereby all under heaven will ascribe benevolence to one," he surely could not have discerned its subtle springs; without Master Yan's utmost strength of resolve, even when given the doctrines that "practicing benevolence depends on oneself" and the "four prohibitions," he surely could not have carried them through with decisive resolution. That the Master imparted this solely to Master Yan was indeed for good reason!

"Without sincerity there would be nothing. Therefore the noble man regards attaining sincerity as precious. Sincerity is not merely the completion of oneself; it is that by which one completes other things."

Li Jin 李瑾

Associate Examiner, Instructor Xu 徐 comments: The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong 中庸) is rooted in the principles of human nature; most candidates in the examination compound wrote in a vague and unfocused manner, and only this essay is thorough in both expression and principle, making it worthy of selection.
Examiner, Instructor Quan 桊 [?] comments: The reasoning is clear and the writing fluent, superior to the crowd of essays.
Examiner, Director of Studies Wu 吳 comments: This essay grasps the purport of Zisi's 子思 discussion of sincerity, and its diction moreover …

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
不冗絕異他作
誠不可無人當實其心誠為己有自然及於物蓋人
心不實則無其物不可不實之也能實其心而自成
焉豈不有以及於物哉且夫誠者真實無妄之謂誠
在於人則為實心人心一有不實則雖有所為亦如
無有如事親不誠於孝則孝之一物無有也事兄不
誠於弟則弟之一物無有也是以君子知不誠則無
是物必以誠之為貴如事親者當實其孝於己焉知
不實則無是事如事兄者當實其弟於己焉蓋人之
===
心能無不實乃為有以自成而道之在我者亦無不
行矣然誠雖所以成己豈徒自成而已哉成不獨成
而自有以成乎物也抑豈但成己而已哉立不獨立
而自有以立乎彼也如孝能自成孝不為己有而彼
亦得以成其孝焉如弟能自成弟不為己私而彼亦
得以成其弟焉蓋誠能成己則自然及物而道亦行
於彼矣誠之為道豈不盡乎抑中庸是章言人道而
以誠論之誠一也在天為實理在人為實心如上文
所謂誠者自成誠者物之終始此以實理言也所謂
punctuated:
不冗，絕異他作。
誠不可無，人當實其心；誠為己有，自然及於物。蓋人心不實，則無其物，不可不實之也；能實其心而自成焉，豈不有以及於物哉？且夫誠者，真實無妄之謂。誠在於人，則為實心；人心一有不實，則雖有所為，亦如無有。如事親不誠於孝，則孝之一物無有也；事兄不誠於弟，則弟之一物無有也。是以君子知不誠則無是物，必以誠之為貴，如事親者當實其孝於己焉；知不實則無是事，如事兄者當實其弟於己焉。蓋人之心能無不實，乃為有以自成，而道之在我者亦無不行矣。然誠雖所以成己，豈徒自成而已哉？成不獨成，而自有以成乎物也；抑豈但成己而已哉？立不獨立，而自有以立乎彼也。如孝能自成，孝不為己有，而彼亦得以成其孝焉；如弟能自成，弟不為己私，而彼亦得以成其弟焉。蓋誠能成己，則自然及物，而道亦行於彼矣。誠之為道，豈不盡乎？抑《中庸》是章言人道而以誠論之。誠，一也，在天為實理，在人為實心。如上文所謂「誠者自成」、「誠者物之終始」，此以實理言也；所謂
translation_en:
…not verbose, utterly distinct from the other compositions.
Sincerity cannot be lacking, so a person ought to make his mind real; once sincerity is possessed within oneself, it naturally extends to other things. For if the human mind is not real, then there are no such things, and so one cannot but make it real; if one can make one's mind real and thereby complete oneself, how could it fail to extend to other things as well? Now, sincerity means that which is genuinely real and free from falsehood. As it exists in a person, sincerity is a real mind; once there is any lack of reality in the human mind, even if one performs some action, it is as though nothing were there. For instance, if in serving one's parents one is not sincere in filial piety, then the thing called filial piety does not exist; if in serving one's elder brother one is not sincere in fraternal respect, then the thing called fraternal respect does not exist. Therefore, the noble man, knowing that without sincerity there is no such thing,必ず values the attainment of sincerity—just as one who serves his parents ought to make filial piety real within himself; knowing that without reality there is no such affair, one who serves his elder brother ought to make fraternal respect real within himself. For when a person's mind can be entirely free from unreality, he thereby has the means to complete himself, and the Way that resides within him will also be practiced without fail. Yet although sincerity is that whereby one completes oneself, how could it merely complete oneself and nothing more? In completing oneself, one does not complete oneself alone, but naturally has the means to complete other things as well; and how could it merely be a matter of completing oneself? In establishing oneself, one does not establish oneself alone, but naturally has the means to establish others as well. For instance, if in filial piety one can complete oneself, filial piety does not remain one's own possession alone, and others too are thereby enabled to complete their filial piety; if in fraternal respect one can complete oneself, fraternal respect does not remain one's private possession alone, and others too are thereby enabled to complete their fraternal respect. For when sincerity is able to complete oneself, it naturally extends to other things, and the Way is practiced among others as well. Is not the Way of sincerity thus exhausted? Furthermore, this chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) speaks of the Way of Man and discusses it in terms of sincerity. Sincerity is one: in Heaven it is real principle, and in man it is a real mind. What the preceding text calls "Sincerity is self-completing" and "Sincerity is the beginning and end of things" is spoken of in terms of real principle; what it calls…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
而道自道與此節言誠此以實心言也然在天者無
不實之理而在人或有不實之心學者果能加誠之
之功則心無不實而在天者在我矣尚其勉之
詩云雨我公田遂及我私惟助為有公田由此
觀之雖周亦助也設為庠序學校以教之庠
者養也校者教也序者射也夏曰校殷曰序
周曰庠學則三代共之皆所以明人倫也
同考試官訓導夏　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕　生昌祚
同考試官訓導吳　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕
考試官教諭□　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕
考試官學正吳　批〔認理明而文足以發之作手也〕
===
告滕君意深矣
大賢之告滕君也既釋詩以見前代養民之制復詳
言以見前代教民之制蓋助法所以養民而庠序學
校所以教民也大賢之於滕君得不舉以告之哉
昔孟子勸文公之行助法故引大田之詩謂天雨我
公田遂及我私蓋公田為君子之養在所當先故農人
punctuated:
「而道自道」與此節言「誠」，此以實心言也。然在天者無不實之理，而在人或有不實之心。學者果能加誠之之功，則心無不實，而在天者在我矣。尚其勉之！

「《詩》云：『雨我公田，遂及我私。』惟助為有公田，由此觀之，雖周亦助也。設為庠、序、學、校以教之：庠者，養也；校者，教也；序者，射也。夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠，學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。」
同考試官訓導夏　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕　生昌祚
同考試官訓導吳　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕
考試官教諭□　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□〕
考試官學正吳　批〔認理明而文足以發之，作手也。〕

告滕君，意深矣。
大賢之告滕君也，既釋《詩》以見前代養民之制，復詳言以見前代教民之制。蓋助法所以養民，而庠、序、學、校所以教民也，大賢之於滕君，得不舉以告之哉？
昔孟子勸文公之行助法，故引《大田》之詩，謂天雨我公田，遂及我私。蓋公田為君子之養，在所當先，故農人
translation_en:
…"and the Way is to be pursued by oneself," along with the discussion of "sincerity" in this section, speaks in terms of a true mind. However, while in Heaven there is no principle that is not true, in man there may sometimes be a mind that is not true. If the student can indeed apply the effort of making it sincere, then his mind will have nothing untrue, and what is in Heaven will be within himself. Let him strive at this!

"The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: 'May it rain on our public fields, and then reach our private ones.' Only under the mutual-aid system (zhu) are there public fields; viewed from this, even the Zhou also used the mutual-aid system. Establish community schools—xiang, xu, xue, and xiao—to instruct them: xiang means nourishing; xiao means instructing; xu means archery. The Xia called them xiao, the Yin called them xu, and the Zhou called them xiang; as for xue, the Three Dynasties shared the name. All of them are the means to clarify human moral relations."
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Xia, comments: [11 illegible characters]. Student: Chang Zuo 昌祚 [?].
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Wu, comments: [11 illegible characters].
Examiner, Instructor [illegible], comments: [11 illegible characters].

…in advising the ruler of Teng, his intention was profound indeed.
When the Great Worthy advised the ruler of Teng, having explained the Book of Odes to show the former dynasties' system of nourishing the people, he again spoke in detail to show the former dynasties' system of instructing the people. For the mutual-aid method (zhufa) is the means to nourish the people, and the xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools are the means to instruct the people; in dealing with the ruler of Teng, how could the Great Worthy fail to bring these up and tell him?
In the past, Mencius (Mengzi) urged Duke Wen to practice the mutual-aid method, and therefore quoted the ode "Large Fields" (Datian), saying that Heaven rains on our public fields and then reaches our private ones. For the public fields provide nourishment for the superior men and ought to come first; therefore the farmers…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
願天之雨必先于𥘉焉私田爲小人之養在所當後
故農人欲雨之降遂及于我焉是惟助法之行而有
此公田之制𢼸令之助法不行久矣由是詩而觀之
則不惟見商之用助而周亦用乎助焉以此詩而驗
之則不惟見殷之行此而周亦行乎此焉前代養民
之制如此君其可不行乎然養民固有以遂其生非
教民則無以復其性故又告以設爲庠序以教之立
爲學校以訓之盖庠以養老爲義校以教民爲義序
以習射爲義鄉學之義固不同也在夏而曰校在殷
===
而曰序在周而曰庠鄉學之名亦有異也以至國學
之名則三代有以共之焉然夏商與周學有大小而
明倫之道無大小之殊庠序學校制有彼此而教民
之意無彼此之間前代教民之制如此君其可不盡
乎吁助法行而民有所養學校立而民有所教孟子
欲滕君之行仁政豈外是哉抑戰國之時王道不明
井田學校不行久矣孟子既告滕君以此而他日又
以經界示畢戰雖當制度已廢之餘能因略以致詳
推舊而爲新不屑屑於既往之迹而能合乎先王之
punctuated: 願天之雨，必先于𥘉焉；私田爲小人之養，在所當後，故農人欲雨之降，遂及于我焉。是惟助法之行，而有此公田之制。𢼸令之助法，不行久矣。由是詩而觀之，則不惟見商之用助，而周亦用乎助焉；以此詩而驗之，則不惟見殷之行此，而周亦行乎此焉。前代養民之制如此，君其可不行乎？然養民固有以遂其生，非教民則無以復其性。故又告以設爲庠序以教之，立爲學校以訓之。盖庠以養老爲義，校以教民爲義，序以習射爲義，鄉學之義固不同也；在夏而曰校，在殷而曰序，在周而曰庠，鄉學之名亦有異也；以至國學之名，則三代有以共之焉。然夏、商與周，學有大小，而明倫之道無大小之殊；庠、序、學、校，制有彼此，而教民之意無彼此之間。前代教民之制如此，君其可不盡乎？吁！助法行而民有所養，學校立而民有所教，孟子欲滕君之行仁政，豈外是哉？抑戰國之時，王道不明，井田、學校不行久矣。孟子既告滕君以此，而他日又以經界示畢戰，雖當制度已廢之餘，能因略以致詳，推舊而爲新，不屑屑於既往之迹，而能合乎先王之…
translation_en: …pray that Heaven's rain must fall there first [?]; the private fields are for the sustenance of the commoners and ought to come second, so the farmers wish for the falling rain to then extend to their own fields. It is only when the mutual-aid tax system (zhufa) is practiced that this institution of public fields exists. Even today [?], the mutual-aid system has long ceased to be practiced. Viewed through this ode, we not only see that the Shang used the mutual-aid system, but that the Zhou used it as well; verified by this ode, we not only see that the Yin practiced this, but that the Zhou practiced it as well. Such was the system of nourishing the people in former dynasties—how could my lord fail to practice it? Yet while nourishing the people indeed enables them to fulfill their livelihoods, without educating the people there is no way to restore their innate nature. Therefore, he further advised establishing community academies (xiang and xu) to educate them, and setting up state and local schools (xue and xiao) to instruct them. For xiang means nourishing the aged, xiao means educating the people, and xu means practicing archery—the meanings of the local schools were indeed different. In the Xia it was called xiao, in the Yin it was called xu, and in the Zhou it was called xiang—the names of the local schools also varied. As for the name of the capital academy (xue), the Three Dynasties shared it in common. Nevertheless, across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou, though schools were greater or lesser in scale, the Way of clarifying human relationships had no distinction between greater and lesser; among xiang, xu, xue, and xiao, though the institutions differed from one another, the intention of educating the people had no divergence between them. Such was the system of educating the people in former dynasties—how could my lord fail to carry it out to the utmost? Ah! When the mutual-aid system is practiced, the people have the means to be nourished; when schools are established, the people have the means to be educated. When Mencius wished the ruler of Teng to practice benevolent governance, how could it be anything beyond this? Moreover, during the Warring States period, the Kingly Way was obscured, and the well-field system and schools had long ceased to be practiced. Mencius having advised the ruler of Teng with this, on another day further explained the defining of field boundaries to Bi Zhan. Even in the aftermath of these institutions having fallen into disuse, he was able to proceed from the rough outline to arrive at the details, extending the old to make it new; without being tied down to the traces of the past, he was able to accord with the [intentions] of the former kings…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
意者真可謂命世亞聖之才矣
易
利有攸往中正有慶
同考試官訓導周　批〔發揮卦體卦辭之旨親切簡當視彼駢儷辭〕〔戾經旨者遠矣宜在選列〕　白震
考試官教諭柴　批〔詞順旨明盖優於易學者也〕
考試官學正吳　批〔發明卦辭深合本義〕
聖人釋卦辭宜往之占必即卦體宜往之善盖慶益
===
之時往无不利所以然者得非由二五之中正有慶
乎宜聖人彖傳發揮以示人也且夫益之爲卦合震
巽而成體文王繫辭以利有攸往而著其占吾夫子
彖傳從而釋之謂夫當損上益下之時民心已說而
無疆吾道既大而且光不有攸往則已往則順理而
行自與吉會无一而不利焉不有攸行則已行則惠
迪之吉勿問可知无一而不宜焉所以然者盖以卦
體二五之中正有慶故爾九五居上體之中而當陽
位之正六二居下體之中而當陰位之正五之應二
punctuated:
意者，真可謂命世亞聖之才矣。

《易》
「利有攸往，中正有慶。」
同考試官訓導周　批：〔發揮卦體、卦辭之旨，親切簡當，視彼駢儷辭〕〔戾經旨者遠矣，宜在選列。〕　白震
考試官教諭柴　批：〔詞順旨明，盖優於《易》學者也。〕
考試官學正吳　批：〔發明卦辭，深合《本義》。〕

聖人釋卦辭宜往之占，必即卦體宜往之善。盖處益之時，往无不利，所以然者，得非由二五之中正有慶乎？宜聖人《彖傳》發揮以示人也。且夫益之爲卦，合震、巽而成體，文王繫辭以「利有攸往」而著其占，吾夫子《彖傳》從而釋之。謂夫當損上益下之時，民心已說而無疆，吾道既大而且光。不有攸往則已，往則順理而行，自與吉會，无一而不利焉；不有攸行則已，行則惠迪之吉，勿問可知，无一而不宜焉。所以然者，盖以卦體二五之中正有慶故爾。九五居上體之中，而當陽位之正；六二居下體之中，而當陰位之正。五之應二，
translation_en:
… the intentions [of the former kings], he can truly be called a world-renowned talent, a Second Sage.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"It is favorable to have somewhere to go; being central and correct, there is celebration." [Tuan commentary on Hexagram 42, Yi (Increase)]
Associate Examiner Zhou, Assistant Instructor, comments: [He brings out the meaning of the hexagram structure and the hexagram statement in a way that is apt, concise, and fitting; compared with those whose parallel-prose verbiage] [violates the purport of the Classic, he is far superior. He ought to be placed among the selected.] — [By candidate] Bai Zhen 白震.
Examiner Chai, Instructor, comments: [The phrasing is smooth and the purport clear; indeed, he is someone accomplished in the study of the Changes.]
Examiner Wu, Subprefectural/Departmental Director of Studies, comments: [His elucidation of the hexagram statement deeply accords with Zhu Xi's Original Meaning (Benyi).]

When the Sage [Confucius] explains the prognostication in the hexagram statement that it is fitting to go forth, he necesariamente bases it upon the goodness in the hexagram's structure that makes it fitting to go forth. Indeed, when dwelling in the time of Increase (Yi,慶益 [sic, for 處益]), there is nothing unfavorable in going forth; as for why this is so, is it not because the second and fifth lines are central and correct, and thus bring celebration? Rightly did the Sage elaborate on this in the Commentary on the Judgments (Tuanzhuan) to show it to people.

Moreover, as a hexagram, Increase combines the trigrams Zhen [Thunder] and Xun [Wind/Wood] to form its structure. King Wen attached the statement "It is favorable to have somewhere to go" to make manifest its prognostication, and our Master [Confucius] in the Commentary on the Judgments accordingly explained it. He meant that at a time of disminuir the above to increase the below, the hearts of the people are already pleased without bound, and our Way is both great and glorious. If one does not go anywhere, there is an end to it; but if one goes forth, one acts in accordance with principle, naturally meeting with good fortune, and there is nothing at all that is not favorable. If one does not undertake any action, there is an end to it; but if one acts, the good fortune of following the right path can be known without even asking, and there is nothing at all that is not fitting. The reason this is so is simply because in the hexagram's structure, the second and fifth lines are central and correct, and thus bring celebration. Nine in the Fifth occupies the center of the upper trigram and matches the correctness of a yang position; Six in the Second occupies the center of the lower trigram and matches the correctness of a yin position. When the fifth responds to the second…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
□以此中正之道二之應五也亦此中正之德二五皆得中正是以明良相逢而君臣得以際君□遇
德澤流行而天下有以受康寧之福升辭利有攸往寧不本於此哉嘗觀易象之諸卦言利往不言利涉益
彖何以兼而有之蓋益以益下爲本本固則無所不利此所以行則利往濟則利涉也大傳曰益以興利
詎不信夫
歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後掛乾
之策二百一十有六坤之策百四十有四凡
三百有六十當期之日
同考試官訓導周　批旌會傳註成文殊勝他作麟騏
出馬群空顧不偉歟
考試官教諭桊　批著法一題衆所易者惟此作得之
考試官學正吳　批能敷出理數之旨亦爲佳作
聖人即歸餘著數以象月之閏合乾坤著數以象歲
之周蓋著策之數與天地之數無往而不合也然甘
出於理勢之自然豈人之智力能損益哉且夫揲著
===
□敖山
punctuated:
□以此中正之道，二之應五也，亦此中正之德。二五皆得中正，是以明良相逢，而君臣得以際君□遇，德澤流行，而天下有以受康寧之福。升辭「利有攸往」，寧不本於此哉？嘗觀《易》象之諸卦，言「利往」不言「利涉」，《益》彖何以兼而有之？蓋益以益下爲本，本固則無所不利，此所以行則利往，濟則利涉也。《大傳》曰：「益以興利。」詎不信夫！

「歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。」
□敖山
同考試官訓導周批：旌會傳註成文，殊勝他作。麟騏出，馬群空，顧不偉歟！
考試官教諭桊批：著法一題，衆所易者，惟此作得之。
考試官學正吳批：能敷出理數之旨，亦爲佳作。

聖人即歸餘著數以象月之閏，合乾坤著數以象歲之周。蓋著策之數，與天地之數，無往而不合也。然甘出於理勢之自然，豈人之智力能損益哉？且夫揲著
translation_en:
… [is] by means of this Way of centrality and correctness; and the second line’s responding to the fifth is likewise by means of this virtue of centrality and correctness. Because both the second and the fifth lines attain centrality and correctness, an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister meet one another, sovereign and subject enjoy a [harmonious] encounter [?], moral grace and beneficence flow forth, and all under heaven receive the blessing of peace and tranquility. Does not the hexagram statement [?] “It is advantageous to have somewhere to go” truly have its root in this? I have observed that among the various hexagrams of the Changes (Yi), some speak of “advantageous to go” without speaking of “advantageous to cross [the great stream]”—why does the Commentary on the Judgment (Tuan) for Increase (Yi) possess both? This is because Increase takes benefiting those below as its root; when the root is firm, there is nothing that is not advantageous. Thus in advancing it is advantageous to go, and in crossing it is advantageous to ford. The Great Treatise (Dazhuan) says, “Increase gives rise to advantage.” How could one not believe this!

“The remainder is placed between the fingers to represent the intercalary month. In five years there are two intercalations; therefore the remainder is twice placed between the fingers and afterward the next [operation of] suspending one [stalk] begins. The stalks of Qian number two hundred and sixteen, and the stalks of Kun number one hundred and forty-four, making three hundred and sixty in all, corresponding to the days of a cycle of the year.”
[…] Ao Shan 敖山
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhou: He brings together [?] the commentaries and annotations to form his essay, far surpassing other compositions. When the unicorn and the thoroughbred appear, the herds of ordinary horses are left behind—is it not magnificent indeed?
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Qin [?]: The topic on the method of yarrow-stalk divination is one that everyone takes lightly [or: finds difficult to master?], yet this composition alone has grasped it.
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wu: Capable of setting forth the essential meaning of principle and number; this too is a fine composition.

The Sage used the number of the remaining yarrow stalks placed between the fingers to represent the intercalary month, and combined the numbers of the yarrow stalks of Qian and Kun to represent the cycle of the year. Indeed, the numbers of the yarrow stalks correspond in every respect with the numbers of Heaven and Earth. Yet all [?] of this arises from the natural spontaneity of principle and tendency—how could human intelligence or strength add to or subtract from it? Now, in the method of counting out yarrow stalks…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
之法既虛而分既掛而揲各有象矣至歸奇於扐復
何所象哉蓋四數兩手之策必有奇餘之數或一二
焉或三四焉左手者歸于第四第三指之間以象夫
三歲之一閏右手者歸于第三第二指之中以象夫
五歲之再閏五歲之中凡有再閏然後別起積分故
五者之中凡有再扐然後別起一掛聖人即歸餘蓍
數以象月之閏者如此若夫揲蓍三變之末餘三奇
則九其過揲之策亦四九三十有六以此計乾之六
爻則得二百一十有六焉餘三□□□過揲之策
===
亦四六□□
有四焉然□□計□□□之策有三百六十之數而周歲
之間由春而夏自秋而冬日亦三百六十而是策足
以當之又非聖人合乾坤蓍數以象歲之周乎雖然
蓍數與造化相準不但是也就此章論之由虛一而
歸奇乃天地四時生萬物者也用奇數策數以定陰
陽老少又萬物各正性命於天地者也吁蓍策造化
妙契无間非翼易聖人發明於大傳其孰能知之
書
punctuated:
之法，既虛而分，既掛而揲，各有象矣。至歸奇於扐，復何所象哉？蓋四數兩手之策，必有奇餘之數，或一、二焉，或三、四焉。左手者，歸于第四、第三指之間，以象夫三歲之一閏；右手者，歸于第三、第二指之中，以象夫五歲之再閏。五歲之中凡有再閏，然後別起積分；故五者之中凡有再扐，然後別起一掛。聖人即歸餘蓍數以象月之閏者如此。若夫揲蓍三變之末，餘三奇則九，其過揲之策亦四九三十有六，以此計乾之六爻，則得二百一十有六焉；餘三□□□過揲之策亦四六□□有四焉。然□□計□□□之策，有三百六十之數，而周歲之間，由春而夏，自秋而冬，日亦三百六十，而是策足以當之，又非聖人合乾坤蓍數以象歲之周乎？雖然，蓍數與造化相準，不但是也。就此章論之，由虛一而歸奇，乃天地四時生萬物者也；用奇數、策數以定陰陽老少，又萬物各正性命於天地者也。吁！蓍策造化，妙契无間，非翼《易》聖人發明於《大傳》，其孰能知之？

《書》
translation_en:
… method [of counting yarrow stalks], once one is set aside and the rest divided, and once one is suspended and the rest counted through by fours, each step already has what it symbolizes. When it comes to placing the remainder between the fingers, what in turn does that symbolize? When counting the stalks in both hands by fours, there must be a remainder of odd or even numbers—either one or two, or else three or four. That from the left hand is placed between the fourth and third fingers, to symbolize one intercalary month in three years; that from the right hand is placed between the third and second fingers, to symbolize two intercalary months in five years. Within five years there are in all two intercalations, and only after that does one start accumulating fractional parts anew; therefore, within the five operations there are in all two placements between the fingers, and only after that does one start a new suspension of a stalk. Such is how the sage takes the yarrow-stalk numbers of the remainders placed between the fingers to symbolize the intercalary months.

As for the end of three transformations in counting yarrow stalks: if there remain three odd lots, that makes nine, and the stalks passed through the counting are four times nine, or thirty-six; reckoning the six lines of Qian by this, one obtains two hundred and sixteen. If there remain three [even lots, that makes six, and][?] the stalks passed through the counting are likewise four times six, [or twenty-][?]four [reckoning the six lines of Kun by this, one obtains one hundred and forty-four][?]. Then, [combining and][?] reckoning the stalks [of the two hexagrams Qian and Kun][?], there is the number three hundred and sixty. And in the course of a full year, from spring to summer and from autumn to winter, the days are also three hundred and sixty, and these stalks are sufficient to correspond to them. Is this not again the sage combining the yarrow-stalk numbers of Qian and Kun to symbolize the cycle of the year?

Even so, the correspondence between yarrow-stalk numbers and the creative transformations of nature does not stop at this alone. Discussing it in terms of this chapter: proceeding from setting one aside to placing the remainder between the fingers is how Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons give birth to the myriad things; using the numbers of the remainders and the numbers of the counted stalks to determine the old and young of yin and yang is in turn how the myriad things each rectify their nature and destiny within Heaven and Earth. Ah! The yarrow stalks and the creative transformations of nature tally with wondrous perfection and without the slightest gap. Had the sage who wrote the Wings to the Book of Changes (Yi) not elucidated this in the Great Commentary (Dazhuan), who would have been able to know it?

Book of Documents (Shu)

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
導沇水東流爲濟入于河溢爲滎東出于陶丘
北又東至于菏又東北會于汶又北東入于海
邢端
同考試官訓導羅　批〔場中作者多以此題爲難是篇深合題意蓋嘗用心於禹貢者歟〕
考試官教諭柴　批〔鋪叙有條筆勢亦着可取〕
考試官學正吳　批〔場中此題詞多艱澁惟是篇順可觀當是作者〕
聖人導濟水於其源之發而順其流之歸也蓋濟
===
水發源於沇而歸宿于海也非聖人濬其源何以得
順流而歸于海哉自今言之治水莫先於隨山亦莫
先於濬川而禹也施濬川之功尤必先於發源之地
焉是故王屋之山泉源所出沇水也濬而滌之則有
以去其壅塞矣然發源爲沇旣東爲濟而入于河濟
水勁疾潛行絕河南溢而爲滎蓋河濟名也而滎即
滎波之滎亭自滎而出于陶丘北濟水至是常見不
伏又東而至于菏蓋陶丘地名也而菏即菏澤之菏
乎濟水至菏豈但止於是哉又東北而會于汶夫濟
punctuated:
「導沇水，東流爲濟，入于河，溢爲滎，東出于陶丘北，又東至于菏，又東北會于汶，又北東入于海。」
邢端
同考試官訓導羅批：〔場中作者多以此題爲難，是篇深合題意，蓋嘗用心於《禹貢》者歟！〕
考試官教諭柴批：〔鋪叙有條，筆勢亦着，可取。〕
考試官學正吳批：〔場中此題詞多艱澁，惟是篇順，可觀，當是作者。〕
聖人導濟水於其源之發，而順其流之歸也。蓋濟水發源於沇，而歸宿于海也。非聖人濬其源，何以得順流而歸于海哉？自今言之，治水莫先於隨山，亦莫先於濬川，而禹也施濬川之功，尤必先於發源之地焉。是故王屋之山，泉源所出，沇水也；濬而滌之，則有以去其壅塞矣。然發源爲沇，旣東爲濟，而入于河；濟水勁疾，潛行絕河，南溢而爲滎。蓋河、濟名也，而滎即滎波之滎亭。自滎而出于陶丘北，濟水至是常見不伏，又東而至于菏。蓋陶丘，地名也，而菏即菏澤之菏乎？濟水至菏，豈但止於是哉？又東北而會于汶。夫濟
translation_en:
"He guided the Yan River, which flowed east to become the Ji and entered the Yellow River; it overflowed to form the Xing, emerged eastward to the north of Taoqiu, went further east to reach the He, went further northeast to join the Wen, and went north and then east to enter the sea."

By Xing Duan 邢端.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Luo 羅: [Most writers in the examination hall found this topic difficult, yet this essay deeply accords with the meaning of the topic. Surely the author is one who has devoted careful study to the "Tribute of Yu" (Yu gong)!]

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Chai 柴: [The exposition is orderly and the momentum of the brush is also forceful; it is worthy of selection.]

Comment by Examiner and Director of Studies Wu 吳: [In the examination hall, the phrasing on this topic was mostly labored and obscure; only this essay flows smoothly and is worth reading. He must be a skilled writer.]

The sage guided the Ji River from where its source springs forth and followed its current to where it returns. For the Ji River has its source in the Yan and finds its final resting place in the sea. Had the sage not dredged its source, how could it have flowed smoothly to return to the sea? Speaking of it today, in controlling the waters nothing took precedence over following the mountains, nor did anything take precedence over dredging the rivers; and when Yu applied his labor of dredging the rivers, he necessarily began first of all at the place where the source sprang forth. Therefore, Mount Wangwu, where the spring source emerges, is the Yan River; by dredging and clearing it, he was able to remove its blockages. Yet, springing forth from its source as the Yan, once it flowed east it became the Ji and entered the Yellow River; because the waters of the Ji are swift and forceful, it traveled underground across the Yellow River, overflowing to the south to form the Xing. Now, the Yellow River and the Ji are names of rivers, and might not the Xing be the Xing of the Xingbo [marsh] [?]? From the Xing it emerged to the north of Taoqiu; having reached this point, the Ji River remained constantly visible and no longer ran underground, going further east until it reached the He. Now, Taoqiu is a place name, and is not the He the He of the Heze [marsh]? When the Ji River reached the He, how could it merely stop there? It went further northeast and joined the Wen. Now, the Ji…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
汶二水昔也固嘗同流而異派今則勢均相敵會合
而為一矣濟水會汶豈終于此哉又東北而入于海
夫海所以納百川向也濟固顯伏而不常今則以小
入大朝宗而有歸矣是則濟水若斷若續而同一其
源流必至于海而後𣏌或見或伏而同一其脉絡必
有所止而後已聖人導水之條例史臣得不詳記之
哉抑考禹貢導水九條或先言山而後水或先言水
而後山說水獨不言山何耶蓋先言山而後水者以
水之源出於山也先言水而後山者以水之源非出
===
於山特自其山以導之耳說水不言山者說水伏流
其出非一故不誌其源也此禹貢立言之法也不可
不知
政貴有恒辭尚體要不惟好異商俗靡靡利口
惟賢餘風未殄公其念哉
同考試官訓導羅　批文詞簡切優於他卷可取
王綸
考試官教諭柴　批理明詞順宜用錄出
考試官學正吳　批題不難作者多纍無失旨璠
punctuated:
汶二水，昔也固嘗同流而異派，今則勢均相敵，會合而為一矣。濟水會汶，豈終于此哉？又東北而入于海。夫海所以納百川，向也濟固顯伏而不常，今則以小入大，朝宗而有歸矣。是則濟水若斷若續，而同一其源流，必至于海而後𣏌；或見或伏，而同一其脉絡，必有所止而後已。聖人導水之條例，史臣得不詳記之哉？抑考《禹貢》導水九條，或先言山而後水，或先言水而後山，說水獨不言山，何耶？蓋先言山而後水者，以水之源出於山也；先言水而後山者，以水之源非出於山，特自其山以導之耳；說水不言山者，說水伏流，其出非一，故不誌其源也。此《禹貢》立言之法也，不可不知。

「政貴有恒，辭尚體要，不惟好異。商俗靡靡，利口惟賢，餘風未殄，公其念哉！」
同考試官訓導羅　批：文詞簡切，優於他卷，可取。
王綸
考試官教諭柴　批：理明詞順，宜用錄出。
考試官學正吳　批：題不難，作者多纍，無失旨璠
translation_en:
… and Wen rivers in the past had indeed flowed together while remaining distinct tributaries, now their forces are equal and matched, converging to become one. Having met the Wen, does the Ji River end here? It goes further northeast and enters the sea. Now, the sea is that which receives the hundred rivers. Previously, the Ji indeed appeared and went underground unpredictably, but now, as the small enters the great, it pays court to the sea and reaches its destination. Thus, although the Ji River seems interrupted and then continuous, its source and course are one and the same, and it does not cease [?] until it reaches the sea; whether visible or subterranean, its veins and channels are one and the same, and it does not stop until it reaches its resting place. How could the historian fail to record in detail the principles by which the sage channeled the waters? Furthermore, if we examine the nine entries on channeling the waters in the "Tribute of Yu" (Yu gong), some mention the mountain first and then the river, while others mention the river first and then the mountain; why does the account of the沇 [transcribed as 說] River alone not mention a mountain? Those that mention the mountain first and then the river do so because the source of the river emerges from that mountain. Those that mention the river first and then the mountain do so because the source of the river does not emerge from that mountain, and it was merely channeled starting from that mountain. That the account of the 沇 [transcribed as 說] River does not mention a mountain is because the 沇 [transcribed as 說] River flows underground and emerges in more than one place, so its source is not recorded. This is the method of composition in the "Tribute of Yu," which one must not fail to know.

"In governance, value consistency; in proclamations, esteem substance and essentials, and do not merelybe fond of novelty. The customs of Shang were extravagant, and sharp-tonguedness alone was considered worthy. Remnants of these ways are not yet extinguished; may you, Duke, bear this in mind!"
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Luo, comments: The writing and diction are concise and to the point, superior to the other papers; it may be selected.
Wang Lun 王綸
Examiner, Instructor Chai, comments: The reasoning is clear and the phrasing smooth; it is suitable to be copied out for publication.
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wu, comments: The topic is not difficult, yet most writers were verbose and convoluted; the only one that neither missed the main purport nor failed in [?]…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
詞順僅見此篇
賢君於大臣也既欲重治體而守常復欲因習俗而
致慮盖治體之大在守常而俗之不美所當慮也聖
君於大臣何其戒之切而望之深歟昔康王命畢公
若曰公亟保釐東郊必有政以乂其民也政必貴於
有恒焉政惟有恒則純清而不擾矣公往撫殷遺民
必有辭以播告于下也辭必尚乎體要焉辭惟體要
則典重而不浮矣然政不可以好異也使其異而是
好則悅須臾而厭持久孰若能有恒乎辭不可以尚
===
異也使其異而是喜則言有餘而理不足孰若能體
要乎矧商之頑民其俗奢靡而盜言孔甘惟以為賢
昔周簡修進良矣其餘風猶不息也公可不為之慮
哉洛之遷民其習流蕩而巧言如簧自以為能令雖
世變風移而遺習猶未泯也公可不為之念哉使誠
能以此為念則政無不成而民無不化此康王所以
望畢公之意歟大抵政令之臧否民俗之美惡皆大
臣一身之繫焉且畢公四世元老德業之隆聞望之
尊何政辭之不善民俗之不可化也康王之致告戒
punctuated:
詞順僅見此篇。
賢君於大臣也，既欲重治體而守常，復欲因習俗而致慮。盖治體之大在守常，而俗之不美所當慮也。聖君於大臣，何其戒之切而望之深歟！昔康王命畢公，若曰：「公亟保釐東郊，必有政以乂其民也，政必貴於有恒焉；政惟有恒，則純清而不擾矣。公往撫殷遺民，必有辭以播告于下也，辭必尚乎體要焉；辭惟體要，則典重而不浮矣。然政不可以好異也，使其異而是好，則悅須臾而厭持久，孰若能有恒乎？辭不可以尚異也，使其異而是喜，則言有餘而理不足，孰若能體要乎？矧商之頑民，其俗奢靡而盜言孔甘，惟以為賢，昔周簡修進良矣，其餘風猶不息也，公可不為之慮哉？洛之遷民，其習流蕩而巧言如簧，自以為能，令雖世變風移，而遺習猶未泯也，公可不為之念哉？」使誠能以此為念，則政無不成，而民無不化，此康王所以望畢公之意歟！大抵政令之臧否，民俗之美惡，皆大臣一身之繫焉。且畢公四世元老，德業之隆，聞望之尊，何政辭之不善、民俗之不可化也？康王之致告戒…
translation_en:
…and smooth phrasing is seen only in this essay.
In dealing with a grand minister, a worthy ruler desires both to attach weight to the principles of governance by upholding constancy, and to exercise forethought in response to prevailing customs. For the greatness of the principles of governance lies in upholding constancy, whereas unseemly customs are what ought to be met with forethought. How earnest was the sage ruler's admonition to his grand minister, and how profound his expectation! In antiquity, when King Kang charged the Duke of Bi, he spoke to this effect: "As you, Duke, go forth to protect and regulate the eastern outskirts, you must have administrative measures with which to govern the people, and in administrative measures, constancy must be prized; only when administrative measures have constancy will they be pure, clear, and unconfusing. As you, Duke, go to pacify the remnant people of Yin, you must have proclamations with which to announce your will to those below, and in proclamations, substance and conciseness must be esteemed; only when proclamations have substance and conciseness will they be dignified, weighty, and free of frivolity. Yet in administration one must not be fond of novelty; if one is fond of novelty, it will please for a moment but grow tiresome over time—how can that compare with being able to maintain constancy? In proclamations one must not esteem novelty; if one delights in novelty, words will be in excess while principle falls short—how can that compare with being able to embody substance and conciseness? Moreover, among the recalcitrant people of Shang, their customs are extravagant and decadent, and deceitful words are considered very sweet, so that they regard only glibness as worthiness. Though in the past Zhou has already selected the cultivated and promoted the good, their lingering habits have still not ceased—how could you, Duke, not give thought to this? Among the relocated people of Luo, their habits are dissolute and their artful words are like reed-organ pipes, taking themselves to be capable. Although the generation has changed and customs have shifted[?], their remnant habits have still not been eradicated—how could you, Duke, not bear this in mind?" If he could truly keep this in mind, then no governance would fail to succeed and no people would fail to be transformed. Was this not the intention behind what King Kang hoped of the Duke of Bi? In general, the goodness or badness of administrative ordinances and the beauty or ugliness of popular customs all hinge upon the person of the grand minister alone. Furthermore, the Duke of Bi was a senior statesman of four reigns, lofty in virtue and achievement, exalted in reputation and prestige—how could his administrative measures and proclamations fail to be good, or the popular customs be impossible to transform? That King Kang delivered his admonition…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
如此厥後道洽政治澤潤生民以收成終之效謂非
得於告戒之力耶
詩
蓺之荏菽荏菽旆旆禾役穟穟麻麥幪幪瓜瓞
唪唪誕后稷之穡有相之道茀厥豐草種之
黃茂
陳鼎
同考試官訓導夏　批〔析理詳明措詞簡當宜居高選〕
考試官學諭榮　批〔平順可取〕
===
考試官學正吳　批〔告后稷當時穡事之詳者有據〕
聖人之種殖地利者致生意之盛聖人之相助地
利者必盡農事之宜夫種殖而致地利之盛者固由
於天性之自然也相助以盡農事之宜者豈非其贊
化育之道乎昔周公制禮尊后稷以配天故推本
而言之若曰后稷當夫岐嶷之時而已好夫種殖之
事其始而種之以荏菽則荏菽之生旆旆然而枝旟
揚起矣繼而樹之以禾稼則禾稼之盛穟穟然而行
列美好矣曰麻曰麥雖彼此之異類莫不幪幪而茂
punctuated:
如此。厥後道洽政治，澤潤生民，以收成終之效，謂非得於告戒之力耶？

詩
蓺之荏菽，荏菽旆旆。禾役穟穟，麻麥幪幪，瓜瓞唪唪。誕后稷之穡，有相之道。茀厥豐草，種之黃茂。
陳鼎
同考試官訓導夏　批〔析理詳明，措詞簡當，宜居高選。〕
考試官學諭榮　批〔平順可取。〕
考試官學正吳　批〔告后稷當時穡事之詳者有據。〕

聖人之種殖地利者，致生意之盛；聖人之相助地利者，必盡農事之宜。夫種殖而致地利之盛者，固由於天性之自然也；相助以盡農事之宜者，豈非其贊化育之道乎？昔周公制禮，尊后稷以配天，故推本而言之。若曰：后稷當夫岐嶷之時，而已好夫種殖之事。其始而種之以荏菽，則荏菽之生，旆旆然而枝旟揚起矣；繼而樹之以禾稼，則禾稼之盛，穟穟然而行列美好矣。曰麻曰麥，雖彼此之異類，莫不幪幪而茂
translation_en:
…in this manner. Thereafter, the Way pervaded and governance was well-ordered, blessings moistened the living people, and the efficacy of bringing things to completion was achieved—could it be said that this was not gained through the power of his admonitions?

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)

"He planted large beans, and the large beans grew waving; his rows of grain were luxuriant, his hemp and wheat dense and thick, his gourds and young melons abundant with fruit. Truly, Hou Ji's husbandry had the way of assisting nature: clearing away the thick grass, he planted the yellow and flourishing grain."

By Chen Ding 陳鼎

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Xia 夏 comments: [The analysis of principle is detailed and clear, and the wording is concise and fitting; he deserves to be placed high on the list of those selected.]
Examiner and Instructor Rong 榮 comments: [Smooth and worthy of selection.]
Examiner and Subdirector of Studies Wu 吳 comments: [His account of the details of Hou Ji's agricultural work at that time is well-grounded.]

When the sage planted and cultivated the bounty of the earth, he brought about flourishing vitality; when the sage assisted the bounty of the earth, he unfailingly exhausted what was proper to agricultural work. Now, planting and cultivating so as to bring about the flourishing of the earth's bounty certainly stemmed from the spontaneity of his heavenly nature; and assisting so as to exhaust what was proper to agricultural work—was this not his way of aiding the transforming and nourishing processes of Heaven and Earth? In ancient times, when the Duke of Zhou instituted the rites, he honored Hou Ji as the correlate of Heaven, and thus traced back to his origins to speak of him. It is as if he said: Even when Hou Ji was still in his perceptive childhood, he already delighted in the work of planting and cultivating. At first, when he planted large beans, the beans grew waving, with their branches and leaves rising up like banners; next, when he set out grain crops, the grain grew luxuriantly, with its rows fine and orderly. Whether hemp or wheat, though different in kind from one another, none failed to grow dense and flourishing…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
窓曰瓜曰瓞雖小大之異名莫不唪唪而多實夫后
稷之種殖如此者非由於習而後能也蓋出於天性
之自然耳夫幼時而好種殖固由其所禀之異及爲
成人而教稼穡又能盡夫人事之宜是以人見其穡
之盛者莫不以爲生物自然之性而不知其能盡人
爲之助也人見其穡之美者莫不以爲天地生成之
功而不知其能盡相助之道也然所以相之者蓋以
豐草之蕪穢所以妨穀者也則必茀治之而後得以
布其嘉穀焉豐草之□□所以害苗者也則必芟刈
===
之而後可以種之□□以爲夫后稷之穡如此者非忽
易而爲之也蓋盡乎人力之助耳抑考思文之詩有
曰粒我烝民莫匪爾極貽我來牟帝命率育凡吾民
得以遂其粒食之願者何莫而非后稷之所賜哉故
帝堯以其有功於民而封於邰也周公制禮尊后稷
以配天而追言及此不亦宜乎
率履不越遂視既發相土烈烈海外有截帝命
不違至于湯齊湯降不遲
朱鼎
punctuated:
窓；曰瓜曰瓞，雖小大之異名，莫不唪唪而多實。夫后稷之種殖如此者，非由於習而後能也，蓋出於天性之自然耳。夫幼時而好種殖，固由其所禀之異；及爲成人而教稼穡，又能盡夫人事之宜。是以人見其穡之盛者，莫不以爲生物自然之性，而不知其能盡人爲之助也；人見其穡之美者，莫不以爲天地生成之功，而不知其能盡相助之道也。然所以相之者，蓋以豐草之蕪穢，所以妨穀者也，則必茀治之，而後得以布其嘉穀焉；豐草之□□，所以害苗者也，則必芟刈之，而後可以種之□□。以爲夫后稷之穡如此者，非忽易而爲之也，蓋盡乎人力之助耳。抑考《思文》之詩有曰：「粒我烝民，莫匪爾極。貽我來牟，帝命率育。」凡吾民得以遂其粒食之願者，何莫而非后稷之所賜哉！故帝堯以其有功於民而封於邰也。周公制禮，尊后稷以配天，而追言及此，不亦宜乎！

「率履不越，遂視既發。相土烈烈，海外有截。帝命不違，至于湯齊。湯降不遲。」

朱鼎
translation_en:
… [luxuriant and] dense [?]; as for the gourds and young melons, though bearing different names for large and small, none failed to be heavily laden and full of fruit. Now, that Hou Ji's planting and cultivating were like this did not come about through practice before he was capable of it; rather, it sprang from the spontaneity of his heavenly nature. That he loved planting and cultivating in childhood was indeed due to his extraordinary endowment; and when he reached adulthood and taught sowing and reaping, he was furthermore able to exhaust what was appropriate in human effort. Therefore, when people saw the abundance of his husbandry, none did not take it to be the natural disposition of living things, not knowing that he was able to exhaust the assistance of human effort; when people saw the excellence of his husbandry, none did not take it to be the generative work of Heaven and Earth, not knowing that he was able to exhaust the way of assisting nature. Yet the way in which he assisted it was that because the rank overgrowth of lush weeds is what hinders the grain, he 반드시 cleared and controlled them before he could spread his fine grain there; and because the [illegible] of lush weeds is what harms the sprouts, he necessarily mowed and cut them down before he could plant the [illegible] [there]. Thus, that Hou Ji's husbandry was like this was not done carelessly or lightly; rather, it exhausted the assistance of human labor. Moreover, examining the ode "Siwen" (Accomplished), it says: "You gave grain to our multitudes of people; / Nothing was not the outcome of your perfection. / You bequeathed to us the wheat and barley, / Which God appointed for the nourishment of all." That all our people have been able to fulfill their desire to eat grain—what part of this is not the gift of Hou Ji? Therefore, Emperor Yao, because of his merit toward the people, enfeoffed him at Tai. When the Duke of Zhou instituted the rites, honoring Hou Ji as the correlate of Heaven, and spoke in retrospect of this, was it not indeed fitting!

"He followed the paths without transgression; / Looking over the people, he saw them forthwith roused to action. / Xiangtu was ardently glorious, / And beyond the seas all was brought into order. / The mandate of God did not fail, / Until in Tang it was completely fulfilled. / Tang's descent was not delayed."

By Zhu Ding 朱鼎

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導吳　批〔場中作者述述不切惟此篇詞簡理明宜取以爲本房之冠〕
考試官教諭柴　批〔旨明詞順宜在高選〕
考試官學正吳　批〔詞簡而意足薦何𢘆〕
君德感人而後王之興廣其業上天眷德而聖人之
生應其時夫德者得天感人之本也今前王之德既
足以感人得天而廣其業矣則聖人之應期而生者
又豈偶然者哉且夫玄王之生也既異於人而其德
也必由乎禮是故動而皆理也有典有則不違乎矩
===
範焉行而皆法也可儀可式不越乎禮度焉是以遂
視其民而民之得於觀感者莫不起而應之以上臨
下而人之獲夫瞻仰者靡不順而從之矣玄王往矣
相土繼之其王業至此時也益烈烈然而光大其國
勢於斯時也愈赫赫然而明顯於是諸侯雖衆無不
帖然而來歸海外雖遠罔不截然而整齊矣夫人心
之所在即天命之所歸是故時雖有先後而皇矣上
帝所以眷顧於有商者不以先後而或殊世雖有遠
近而彼蒼者天所以默契於商家者不以久遠而或
punctuated:
同考試官訓導吳　批：〔場中作者述述不切，惟此篇詞簡理明，宜取以爲本房之冠。〕
考試官教諭柴　批：〔旨明詞順，宜在高選。〕
考試官學正吳　批：〔詞簡而意足，薦何𢘆。〕

君德感人，而後王之興廣其業；上天眷德，而聖人之生應其時。夫德者，得天感人之本也。今前王之德，既足以感人得天而廣其業矣，則聖人之應期而生者，又豈偶然者哉？且夫玄王之生也，既異於人；而其德也，必由乎禮。是故動而皆理也，有典有則，不違乎矩範焉；行而皆法也，可儀可式，不越乎禮度焉。是以遂視其民，而民之得於觀感者，莫不起而應之；以上臨下，而人之獲夫瞻仰者，靡不順而從之矣。玄王往矣，相土繼之，其王業至此時也，益烈烈然而光大；其國勢於斯時也，愈赫赫然而明顯。於是諸侯雖衆，無不帖然而來歸；海外雖遠，罔不截然而整齊矣。夫人心之所在，即天命之所歸。是故時雖有先後，而皇矣上帝所以眷顧於有商者，不以先後而或殊；世雖有遠近，而彼蒼者天所以默契於商家者，不以久遠而或
