title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
為仁由己而由人乎哉顏淵曰請問其目
子曰非禮勿視非禮勿聽非禮勿言
非禮勿動
不誠無物是故君子誠之為貴誠者非自
成己而已也所以成物也
詩云雨我公田遂及我私惟助為有公田
===
由此觀之雖周亦助也設為庠序學
校以教之庠者養也校者教也序者
射也夏曰校殷曰序周曰庠學則三
代共之皆所以明人倫也
易
六三觀我生進退象曰觀我生進退未失
道也六四觀國之光利用賓于王象
曰觀國之光尚賓也
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

「為仁由己，而由人乎哉？」顏淵曰：「請問其目。」子曰：「非禮勿視，非禮勿聽，非禮勿言，非禮勿動。」

不誠無物。是故君子誠之為貴。誠者，非自成己而已也，所以成物也。

《詩》云：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」惟助為有公田。由此觀之，雖周亦助也。設為庠、序、學、校以教之。庠者，養也；校者，教也；序者，射也。夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠，學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。

易

六三：觀我生進退。《象》曰：「觀我生進退」，未失道也。六四：觀國之光，利用賓于王。《象》曰：「觀國之光」，尚賓也。
translation_en:
First Session

The Four Books

"The practice of benevolence depends on oneself; how could it depend on others?" Yan Yuan said, "I beg to ask for the steps of this process." The Master said, "Look not at what is contrary to ritual propriety; listen not to what is contrary to ritual propriety; speak not what is contrary to ritual propriety; make no movement that is contrary to ritual propriety."

Without sincerity there would be nothing. Therefore, the noble man regards the attainment of sincerity as the most precious thing. Sincerity is not merely the completion of oneself; it is that by which one completes other things as well.

The Book of Odes (Shi) says: "May it rain first on our public fields, and then come to our private ones." Only under the mutual-aid (zhu) system were there public fields. Viewed from this perspective, even the Zhou dynasty also practiced the mutual-aid system. They established xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools to instruct the people. Xiang means to nourish; xiao means to teach; xu means to practice archery. The Xia dynasty called them xiao, the Yin dynasty called them xu, and the Zhou dynasty called them xiang; as for xue, all Three Dynasties shared the name. All of them served to clarify human relationships.

Classic of Changes (Yi)

Six in the third place: Contemplating my own life, to advance or retreat. The Commentary on the Images (Xiang) says: "'Contemplating my own life, to advance or retreat'—one has not yet lost the Way." Six in the fourth place: Contemplating the glory of the state, it is fitting to be the guest of the king. The Commentary on the Images says: "'Contemplating the glory of the state'—guests are esteemed."

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
利有攸往中正有慶
歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後
掛乾之策二百一十有六坤之策百
四十有四凡三百有六十當期之日
理財正辭禁民為非曰義
書
導沇水東流為濟入于河溢為滎東出于
陶丘北又東至于菏又東北會于汶
又北東入于海
===
亦越文王武王克知三有宅心灼見三有
俊心以敬事上帝立民長伯立政任
人準夫牧作三事虎賁綴衣趣馬小
尹左右攜僕百司庶府大都小伯藝
人表臣百司太史尹伯庶常吉士
政貴有恒辭尚體要不惟好異商俗靡靡
利口惟賢餘風未殄公其念哉
punctuated:
利有攸往，中正有慶。
歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。
理財正辭，禁民為非曰義。
《書》：
導沇水，東流為濟，入于河，溢為滎，東出于陶丘北，又東至于菏，又東北會于汶，又北東入于海。
亦越文王、武王，克知三有宅心，灼見三有俊心，以敬事上帝，立民長伯。立政：任人、準夫、牧，作三事；虎賁、綴衣、趣馬、小尹，左右攜僕、百司，庶府，大都、小伯、藝人、表臣百司，太史、尹伯、庶常吉士。
政貴有恒，辭尚體要，不惟好異。商俗靡靡，利口惟賢，餘風未殄，公其念哉！
translation_en:
"It is favorable to have somewhere to go": through centrality and correctness there is blessing.
The remainder is placed between the fingers to symbolize the intercalary month. In five years there are two intercalations, and therefore the stalks are placed between the fingers twice and afterward set aside. The stalks of Qian number two hundred and sixteen, and the stalks of Kun number one hundred and forty-four, making three hundred and sixty in all, corresponding to the days of a cycle of the year.
Ordering wealth, rectifying speech, and prohibiting the people from doing wrong is called rightness.
Book of Documents (Shu):
He channeled the Yan River; flowing eastward it became the Ji, entered the Yellow River, overflowed to form the Xing marsh, emerged eastward to the north of Taoqiu, went further east to the He marsh, went further northeast to join the Wen River, and then went north and east to enter the sea.
And when it came to King Wen and King Wu, they were able to know the minds of those in the three positions and clearly perceive the minds of those of the three grades of excellence, so as to reverently serve the Lord on High and establish leaders and chiefs for the people. In establishing government: the Renren (wardens), Zhunfu (law-officers), and Mu (pastors) acted as the Three Affairs; there were the Huben (tiger braves), Zhuiyi (keepers of the robes), Quma (equerries), and Xiaoyin (lesser directors); the attendants who carry implements on the left and right and the hundred officials; the various storehouse keepers; the chiefs of large cities, the chiefs of small cities, the artisans, the exterior officials and their hundred offices; and the Taishi (Grand Scribe), the Yinbo (directors and chiefs), and the many constant and worthy gentlemen.
In governance one prizes constancy; in proclamations one values substance and conciseness, not a fondness for novelty. The customs of Shang were extravagant, esteeming onlyglibness of tongue as worthiness, and the lingering influences have not yet been extinguished; Your Grace, be mindful of this!

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
其刑其罰其審克之
詩
孑孑干旄在浚之郊素絲紕之良馬四之
彼姝者子何以畀之孑孑干旟在浚
之都素絲組之良馬五之彼姝者子
何以予之孑孑干旌在浚之城素絲
祝之良馬六之彼姝者子何以告之
天立厥配受命既固
===
蓺之荏菽荏菽旆旆禾役穟穟麻麥幪幪
瓜瓞唪唪誕后稷之穡有相之道茀
厥豐草種之黃茂
率履不越遂視既發相土烈烈海外有截
帝命不違至于湯齊湯降不遲
春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕滕子來朝〔桓公二年〕荊人來聘
〔莊公二十三年〕公會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭
punctuated:
其刑其罰，其審克之。

詩
孑孑干旄，在浚之郊。素絲紕之，良馬四之。彼姝者子，何以畀之？孑孑干旟，在浚之都。素絲組之，良馬五之。彼姝者子，何以予之？孑孑干旌，在浚之城。素絲祝之，良馬六之。彼姝者子，何以告之？
天立厥配，受命既固。
蓺之荏菽，荏菽旆旆。禾役穟穟，麻麥幪幪，瓜瓞唪唪。誕后稷之穡，有相之道。茀厥豐草，種之黃茂。
率履不越，遂視既發。相土烈烈，海外有截。帝命不違，至于湯齊。湯降不遲。

春秋
春王正月〔隱公元年〕；滕子來朝〔桓公二年〕；荊人來聘〔莊公二十三年〕；公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭
translation_en:
“In punishments and in fines, examine them carefully and master them.”

Book of Odes (Shi):
“Conspicuously rises the staff with its ox-tail crest, in the suburbs of Xun; bound with white silk bands, with a team of four fine horses. That admirable gentleman—what shall I give to him? Conspicuously rises the staff with its falcon banner, in the outer districts of Xun; braided with white silk cords, with a team of five fine horses. That admirable gentleman—what shall I present to him? Conspicuously rises the staff with its feathered pennon, by the city wall of Xun; woven with white silk threads, with a team of six fine horses. That admirable gentleman—what counsel shall I offer him?”
“Heaven established its mate for him, and the mandate he received became firmly secured.”
“He planted large beans, and the large beans grew luxuriant and waving; the rows of grain were heavy in the ear, the hemp and wheat were dense and thick, and the gourds and melons were clustered in abundance. Truly, Hou Ji’s husbandry followed the way of assisting nature; having cleared away the thick grass, he sowed the yellow, thriving grain.”
“Following the path without transgression, he looked out upon them and all responded. Xiangtu was glorious and martial, and beyond the seas all was brought into order. The mandate of the Supreme Sovereign did not fail, down to Tang, with whom it was fulfilled. Tang’s descent was not delayed.”

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
“In spring, the king’s first month” [First year of Duke Yin]; “The Viscount of Teng came to court” [Second year of Duke Huan]; “A man of Jing came on a mission of friendly inquiry” [Twenty-third year of Duke Zhuang]; “The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the [Earl of] Zheng…”

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
伯衛子莒子盟于踐土　公朝于王所
〔僖公二十八年〕天王使宰周公來聘〔僖公三十
年〕
王人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕公會王人齊侯宋公衛侯
許男曹伯陳世子款盟于洮〔僖公八年〕會王
人晉人宋人齊人陳人蔡人秦人盟于翟泉
〔僖公二十九年〕
宋公齊侯□□□□江〔莊公三十二年〕齊侯宋公江人
黃人盟于貫〔僖公二年〕齊侯宋公江人黃人會
于陽穀〔僖公三年〕遂伐楚　楚屈完來盟
于師　盟于召陵　齊人執陳轅濤塗
===
及江人黃人伐陳　公孫茲帥師會齊人宋
人衛人鄭人許人曹人侵陳〔僖公四年〕公及
齊侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯會
王世子于首止　諸侯盟于首止　鄭伯逃
歸不盟　楚人滅弦〔僖公五年〕楚人圍許
punctuated:
伯、衛子、莒子盟于踐土。公朝于王所。〔僖公二十八年〕天王使宰周公來聘。〔僖公三十年〕
王人子突救衛。〔莊公六年〕公會王人、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、許男、曹伯、陳世子款盟于洮。〔僖公八年〕會王人、晉人、宋人、齊人、陳人、蔡人、秦人盟于翟泉。〔僖公二十九年〕
宋公、齊侯□□□□江。〔莊公三十二年〕齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人盟于貫。〔僖公二年〕齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕遂伐楚。楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。齊人執陳轅濤塗。及江人、黃人伐陳。公孫茲帥師會齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭人、許人、曹人侵陳。〔僖公四年〕公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會王世子于首止。諸侯盟于首止，鄭伯逃歸不盟。楚人滅弦。〔僖公五年〕楚人圍許。
translation_en:
… the Earl of [Zheng], the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju made a covenant at Jiantu. The Duke paid court at the King's temporary residence. [28th year of Duke Xi.] The Heavenly King sent the Grand Administrator, the Duke of Zhou, to come on a mission of friendly inquiry. [30th year of Duke Xi.]
The King's man Zitu went to the rescue of Wei. [6th year of Duke Zhuang.] The Duke met with the King's man, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Kuan, Heir Apparent of Chen, and made a covenant at Tao. [8th year of Duke Xi.] [Someone] met with the King's man, an officer of Jin, an officer of Song, an officer of Qi, an officer of Chen, an officer of Cai, and an officer of Qin, and made a covenant at Diquan. [29th year of Duke Xi.]
The Duke of Song and the Marquis of Qi [met at Liangqiu (?)]. [32nd year of Duke Zhuang.] The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, an officer of Jiang, and an officer of Huang made a covenant at Guan. [2nd year of Duke Xi.] The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, an officer of Jiang, and an officer of Huang met at Yanggu. [3rd year of Duke Xi.] Thereupon they invaded Chu. Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army, and made a covenant at Shaoling. The men of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen. Together with the men of Jiang and the men of Huang, [the Duke] invaded Chen. Gongsun Zi led a force to join the men of Qi, the men of Song, the men of Wei, the men of Zheng, the men of Xu, and the men of Cao in making an incursion into Chen. [4th year of Duke Xi.] The Duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the King's Heir Apparent at Shouzhi. The feudal lords made a covenant at Shouzhi; the Earl of Zheng fled home without joining the covenant. The men of Chu extinguished Xian. [5th year of Duke Xi.] The men of Chu besieged Xu. …

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
僖公六年
季孫行父臧孫許叔孫僑如公孫嬰齊帥師會晉
郤克衛孫良夫曹公子首及齊侯戰于鞌
成公二年　季孫宿叔老會晉士匄齊人宋人
衛人鄭公孫蠆曹人莒人邾人滕人薛人杞人小
邾人會吳于向〔襄公十四年〕
禮記
制三公一命卷若有加則賜也不過九命
===
射之以樂也何以聽何以射
閏月則闔門左扉立于其中皮弁以日視朝
遂以食日中而餕奏而食日少牢朔月大
牢五飲上水漿酒醴酏
然則先王之爲樂也以法治也善則行象德
矣
第貳場
論
punctuated:
〔僖公六年〕。
季孫行父、臧孫許、叔孫僑如、公孫嬰齊帥師，會晉郤克、衛孫良夫、曹公子首，及齊侯戰于鞌〔成公二年〕。季孫宿、叔老會晉士匄、齊人、宋人、衛人、鄭公孫蠆、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人，會吳于向〔襄公十四年〕。

《禮記》：
制：三公一命卷；若有加，則賜也，不過九命。
射之以樂也，何以聽？何以射？
閏月，則闔門左扉，立于其中。皮弁以日視朝，遂以食。日中而餕，奏而食。日少牢，朔月大牢。五飲：上水、漿、酒、醴、酏。
然則先王之爲樂也，以法治也，善則行象德矣。

第貳場
論
translation_en:
… [6th year of Duke Xi 僖公].

Jisun Xingfu 季孫行父, Zangsun Xu 臧孫許, Shusun Qiaoru 叔孫僑如, and Gongsun Yingqi 公孫嬰齊 led a force to join Xi Ke 郤克 of Jin 晉, Sun Liangfu 孫良夫 of Wei 衛, and Gongzi Shou 公子首 of Cao 曹, and fought with the Marquis of Qi 齊 at An 鞌 [2nd year of Duke Cheng 成公]. Jisun Su 季孫宿 and Shu Lao 叔老 met with Shi Gai 士匄 of Jin, an officer of Qi, an officer of Song 宋, an officer of Wei, Gongsun Chai 公孫蠆 of Zheng 鄭, an officer of Cao, an officer of Ju 莒, an officer of Zhu 邾, an officer of Teng 滕, an officer of Xue 薛, an officer of Qi 杞, and an officer of Little Zhu 小邾, and met with Wu 吳 at Xiang 向 [14th year of Duke Xiang 襄公].

Record of Rites (Liji 禮記):

According to the regulations, the Three Dukes (Sangong 三公), if advanced one degree of appointment, wear the dragon robe (juan 卷); if there is any further addition, it is by special bestowal, not exceeding nine degrees of appointment.

In shooting to the accompaniment of music, how does one manage both to listen to the music and to hit the mark in shooting?

In an intercalary month, he closes the left leaf of the door and stands in the middle of the doorway. Wearing the white deerskin cap, he holds daily court and then takes his meal. At midday he eats the remains of the morning meal, eating to the playing of music. Daily there is the lesser offering of a sheep and a pig (shaolao 少牢), and on the first day of the month the great offering of an ox, a sheep, and a pig (tailao 大牢). For the five drinks, water is placed first, along with sour rice-water, wine, sweet wine, and thin porridge.

Thus the former kings, in instituting music, used it as a model for governance; when it is good, the conduct of the people comes to resemble their virtue.

Second Session

Discourse…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
德主天下之善
詔誥表〔內科一道〕

擬唐以陸贄為中書侍郎同平章事誥
擬
車駕幸太學謝表

承差轉雇寄人
詐欺官私取財

策五道
問自古帝王欽慎刑法盖以法者人之命
刑者國之養苟或失其科條固難以措

「德主天下之善。」

擬漢章帝會諸儒白虎觀議《五經》同異詔。
擬唐以陸贄為中書侍郎同平章事誥。

策五道

問：自古帝王欽慎刑法，盖以法者人之命，刑者國之養，苟或失其科條，固難以措
translation_en:
"Virtue presides over the goodness of all under Heaven."

Imperial Edict, Patent of Appointment, and Memorial [examined on one topic from among these]:
An imitation of Emperor Zhang of Han's edict convening the Confucian scholars at the White Tiger Hall (Baihu guan) to deliberate on the similarities and differences among the Five Classics.
An imitation of the Tang patent appointing Lu Zhi陸贄 as Vice Director of the Secretariat (Zhongshu shilang) and Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery (Tong pingzhangshi).
An imitation of a memorial of gratitude upon the Imperial Carriage visiting the Directorate of Education (Taixue).

Legal Judgments [five items]:
Recommending and employing officials or subofficial functionaries who have committed offenses.
Purchasing land and residences at the place of one's official post.
Prohibiting spirit mediums and heterodox arts.
Couriers sub-hiring others or entrusting their dispatches to others.
Defrauding government agencies or private individuals to obtain property.

Third Session

Five Policy Questions

Question: Since antiquity, emperors and kings have been reverent and cautious regarding penal law. This is because laws are the lifeblood of the people, and punishments are what nourish the state [?]; if the statutory articles lose their proper measure, the people will truly have nowhere to place…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
手足矣恭惟我
太祖高皇帝
御極之初即
命詳定律法
太宗文皇帝繼體守成亦許寃抑自陳
皇宗章皇帝又製五倫書須行天下而於君道
篇悉載古今慎刑之意以昭鑒戒
聖德好生何其至歟然恤刑之條始之以何人
===
之言終之以何人之說下車泣囚其與
刑期于無刑之心同與異與納隍致慮
其與好生之德協與否與刑罰不中則
民無所措手足者其言何三見與死者
不可復生其語何四出與今
皇上明德慎罰屢詔恤刑固將與
祖宗同一盛心矣諸士子佩服
聖訓蓋亦有年他日倘為掌刑之官必將有以
punctuated: 手足矣。恭惟我太祖高皇帝御極之初，即命詳定律法；太宗文皇帝繼體守成，亦許寃抑自陳；皇宗章皇帝又製《五倫書》須行天下，而於〈君道篇〉悉載古今慎刑之意，以昭鑒戒。聖德好生，何其至歟！然〈恤刑〉之條，始之以何人之言，終之以何人之說？下車泣囚，其與「刑期于無刑」之心同與異與？納隍致慮，其與「好生之德」協與否與？「刑罰不中，則民無所措手足」者，其言何三見與？「死者不可復生」，其語何四出與？今皇上明德慎罰，屢詔恤刑，固將與祖宗同一盛心矣。諸士子佩服聖訓，蓋亦有年，他日倘為掌刑之官，必將有以
translation_en: … hands and feet. Reverently considering our Grand Progenitor the Lofty Emperor (Taizu, the Hongwu Emperor), at the very beginning of his ascension to the throne he immediately ordered the detailed codification of the laws. When the Grand Ancestor the Cultured Emperor (Taizong, the Yongle Emperor) succeeded to the body of the state and preserved the achievements, he likewise permitted those suffering冤屈 (wrongful grievances) to state their cases themselves. The Imperial Ancestor [?皇宗, sc. Xuanzong 宣宗] the Brilliant Emperor (the Xuande Emperor) further compiled the Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) and promulgated [?須, sc. 頒] it throughout the realm, and in its "Chapter on the Way of the Ruler" (Jundao pian) he fully recorded the intentions of ancient and modern times regarding circumspection in punishments, so as to display a mirror of warning. The sacred virtue of loving life—how supreme it is! Yet in the section on "Compassion in Punishments" (Xuxing), with whose words does it begin, and with whose discourse does it conclude? Alighting from the carriage to weep over prisoners—is this the same as or different from the mind that "uses punishments in the hope of ending punishments"? Feeling anxiety as if pushing people into a dry moat—does this accord with "the virtue of loving life" or not? Why does the saying "If punishments and penalties miss the mark, the people have nowhere to place their hands and feet" appear three times therein? And why does the phrase "The dead cannot be brought back to life" occur four times therein? Now His Majesty the Emperor makes bright his virtue and is circumspect in penalties, repeatedly issuing edicts on compassion in punishments; truly he shares the same magnificent heart as the imperial ancestors. You gentlemen have cherished and abided by the sacred instructions for some years now; if on another day you should become officials in charge of punishments, you will surely have a way to…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
處之者願著于篇
問大學中庸聖賢傳授心法之書其言雖
博而誠敬二者足以該之夫敬爲大學
之要領何至傳三章始言緝熙敬止未
知此章之前亦有敬可言歟誠爲中庸
之樞紐何至十六章始言誠不可揜未
知此章之前亦有誠可指歟敬之釋先
儒有言主一無適者有言整齊嚴肅者
===
有言常惺惺法者又有言收斂不容一
物者四言之中奚爲至切誠之釋先儒
有以不欺爲言者有以不息爲言者有
以無妄爲言者又有以真實無妄爲言
者四語之中奚爲至要夫誠敬既爲庸
學之要學者欲從事於誠敬果當交致
其功歟抑或有先後緩急歟誠敬之說
亦未知始於何經歟願詳著之以觀居
punctuated:
處之者，願著于篇。
問：《大學》、《中庸》，聖賢傳授心法之書，其言雖博，而「誠」、「敬」二者足以該之。夫「敬」爲《大學》之要領，何至傳三章始言「緝熙敬止」？未知此章之前，亦有「敬」可言歟？「誠」爲《中庸》之樞紐，何至十六章始言「誠不可揜」？未知此章之前，亦有「誠」可指歟？「敬」之釋，先儒有言「主一無適」者，有言「整齊嚴肅」者，有言「常惺惺法」者，又有言「收斂不容一物」者，四言之中，奚爲至切？「誠」之釋，先儒有以「不欺」爲言者，有以「不息」爲言者，有以「無妄」爲言者，又有以「真實無妄」爲言者，四語之中，奚爲至要？夫「誠」、「敬」既爲《庸》、《學》之要，學者欲從事於「誠」、「敬」，果當交致其功歟？抑或有先後緩急歟？「誠」、「敬」之說，亦未知始於何經歟？願詳著之，以觀居
translation_en:
… deal with them; I hope you will set this forth in your essay.

Question: The Great Learning (Daxue) and the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) are books through which the sages and worthies transmitted the method of the mind. Although their words are wide-ranging, the two concepts of "sincerity" (cheng) and "reverent seriousness" (jing) are sufficient to encompass them. Now, reverent seriousness is the essential guiding principle of the Great Learning; why is it that only in the third chapter of the commentary does it first speak of "continuing bright and reverently resting"? Before this chapter, is there also anything that can be spoken of as reverent seriousness? Sincerity is the pivot of the Doctrine of the Mean; why is it that only in the sixteenth chapter does it first say that "sincerity cannot be concealed"? Before this chapter, is there also anything that can be pointed to as sincerity? As for the explanation of reverent seriousness, among former Confucian scholars there was one who spoke of "concentrating on one thing without departing from it," one who spoke of "being orderly, composed, stern, and solemn," one who spoke of "the method of remaining constantly alert and awake," and another who spoke of "gathering in the mind and not allowing a single thing to intrude." Among these four statements, which is the most pertinent? As for the explanation of sincerity, among former Confucian scholars there was one who spoke of it in terms of "no self-deception," one who spoke of it in terms of "ceaselessness," one who spoke of it in terms of "freedom from falsity," and another who spoke of it in terms of "being true, real, and free from falsity." Among these four phrases, which is the most essential? Since sincerity and reverent seriousness are the essentials of the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning, if a student wishes to apply himself to sincerity and reverent seriousness, should he indeed devote effort to both mutually, or is there an order of priority and urgency between them? Furthermore, in which Classic did the doctrines of sincerity and reverent seriousness first originate? Please set this forth in detail, so that we may observe your learning in abiding in …

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
敬立誠之學
問明經進士兩科自隋唐以來而始盛論
者謂唐重明經而輕進士宋重進士而
輕明經何以知其然歟唐有欲罷明經
進士之科者其所以欲罷之意可得而
言歟其試之之法有以詩賦論策而復
加以經義之制者則自何時而立有臨
軒試以詩賦而復定以策試之制者則
===
自何時而始且糊名易書之制旣立而
諸州之糊名易書則始於何時而易書
則又從何人請歟如傳義匿服之有禁
冒貫挾書之有條抑因何事而舉歟封
印卷首嚴禁秉燭又因何人之言而行
歟若受知先朝擢自下第偉有儀狀擢
居首選者可知其人歟又若懷州發解
素已銓次大名舉子自相推先者其人
punctuated:
敬立誠之學。
問：明經、進士兩科，自隋、唐以來而始盛。論者謂唐重明經而輕進士，宋重進士而輕明經，何以知其然歟？唐有欲罷明經、進士之科者，其所以欲罷之意可得而言歟？其試之之法，有以詩賦、論、策而復加以經義之制者，則自何時而立？有臨軒試以詩賦而復定以策試之制者，則自何時而始？且糊名、易書之制旣立，而諸州之糊名、易書則始於何時？而易書則又從何人請歟？如傳義、匿服之有禁，冒貫、挾書之有條，抑因何事而舉歟？封印卷首、嚴禁秉燭，又因何人之言而行歟？若受知先朝、擢自下第，偉有儀狀、擢居首選者，可知其人歟？又若懷州發解、素已銓次，大名舉子、自相推先者，其人
translation_en:
… learning of dwelling in reverence and establishing sincerity.
Question: The two examination categories of Classicist (mingjing) and Metropolitan Graduate (jinshi) first flourished from the Sui and Tang dynasties onward. Commentators say that the Tang valued the Classicist category and slighted the Metropolitan Graduate, whereas the Song valued the Metropolitan Graduate and slighted the Classicist; how do we know this to be so? In the Tang, there were those who wished to abolish the Classicist and Metropolitan Graduate categories; can the reasons why they wished to abolish them be stated? As for the methods of examining them, when was the system established that tested with regulated verse and rhapsodies (shifu), discourses (lun), and policy questions (ce), and then further added explications of the Classics (jingyi)? And when did the system begin in which the emperor personally presided over examinations using regulated verse and rhapsodies, and then settled on testing with policy questions? Moreover, once the systems of sealing candidates' names (huming) and transcribing examination papers (yishu) were established, when did the sealing of names and transcribing of papers in the various prefectures begin? And at whose request was the transcribing of papers adopted? On account of what events were the prohibitions against passing along model expositions and concealing mourning obligations, or the regulations against falsifying native registration and smuggling in books, instituted? And on account of whose words were sealing and stamping the head of the examination paper and strictly prohibiting the holding of candles at night put into practice? As for the one who had gained the recognition of a previous reign and was promoted after failing the examination, and the one of imposing appearance who was elevated to first place—can those persons be identified? Or again, in the case where Huaizhou forwarded its recommended candidates whose ranking had already been determined beforehand, and the case where the candidates of Daming yielded precedence to one another of their own accord—can those persons…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
亦可考歟諸士子於科目必嘗究其實
矣請悉以對
問理學類編一書皆集先儒之格言而示
學者以窮理之要也姑舉其槩以質之
夫編集是書固有次第而其目可歷陳
歟講論太極固非一人而精微孰為得
歟天地有闔闢驗之於何物天一而生
水徵之於何事陽唱陰和則雨亦有雨
===
風而雨者何地歟陰陽氣和乃雨亦有
龍能致之者何義歟雷本氣也或擊人
與物而成斧石者果神物所主歟電亦
氣也或閃爍激疾如金蛇飛騰之狀者
何形氣若是歟論陰陽則有以象類言
有以動靜言有以對待言又有以錯綜
言者何不同歟論五行則有以質而語
其生之序有以氣而語其行之序有統
punctuated:
亦可考歟？諸士子於科目，必嘗究其實矣，請悉以對。

問：《理學類編》一書，皆集先儒之格言，而示學者以窮理之要也。姑舉其槩以質之。夫編集是書，固有次第，而其目可歷陳歟？講論太極，固非一人，而精微孰為得歟？天地有闔闢，驗之於何物？天一而生水，徵之於何事？陽唱陰和則雨，亦有雨風而雨者，何地歟？陰陽氣和乃雨，亦有龍能致之者，何義歟？雷本氣也，或擊人與物而成斧石者，果神物所主歟？電亦氣也，或閃爍激疾如金蛇飛騰之狀者，何形氣若是歟？論陰陽，則有以象類言，有以動靜言，有以對待言，又有以錯綜言者，何不同歟？論五行，則有以質而語其生之序，有以氣而語其行之序，有統
translation_en:
…can those persons also be verified? You gentlemen have surely investigated the actual facts regarding the examination system; please respond in full detail.

Question: The book Classified Compilation on the Study of Principle (Lixue leibian 理學類編) collects the maxims of former Confucians in order to show scholars the essentials of fathoming principle. Let us raise its general outlines to examine you. The compilation of this book certainly follows a sequence; can its headings be enumerated one by one? Those who have discussed the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji 太極) are certainly not just a single person; who has grasped its subtle essence? Heaven and Earth have their closing and opening; by what things is this verified? "Heaven is One and generates Water"; by what affairs is this evidenced? When yang leads and yin harmonizes, it rains, yet there is also a place where it rains whenever there is rain-wind [?]; what place is that? Only when the qi of yin and yang are in harmony does it rain, yet dragons are also able to bring it about; what is the principle behind this? Thunder is fundamentally qi, yet sometimes it strikes people and things and forms axe-shaped stones; is this truly governed by divine beings? Lightning is also qi, yet sometimes it flashes and darts rapidly in the form of a leaping golden snake; why are its form and qi like this? In discussing yin and yang, some speak of them in terms of emblematic categories, some in terms of movement and stillness, some in terms of opposition and complementarity, and some in terms of intertwining and alternation; why do they differ? In discussing the Five Phases (wuxing 五行), some speak of the sequence of their generation in terms of material substance, some speak of the sequence of their operation in terms of qi, some…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
而言之者又有錯而言之者何相異歟
願著于篇以觀窮理之學
問
國家承平之時亦不可忘武備也武備脩則
教閱有方講習有素萬一不虞用之以
禦侮銷患無難事矣稽之成周四時講
武所謂振旅茇舍治兵大閱是已其制
可得而詳歟秦不師古盜由廢炎漢
===
之興内則有東之之制外則有都試之
名李唐之世府兵有一時之講顯德有
習射之較并州城北驪山之下又相
有講焉至于有宋四時有講武之儀而
郊行大閱之禮朱明之池講武之殿亦
相繼有習焉可各指其實而陳之歟抑
有優劣之可議歟其亦有合於成周之
制否歟逮于我
punctuated:
而言之者，又有錯而言之者，何相異歟？願著于篇，以觀窮理之學。
問：國家承平之時，亦不可忘武備也。武備脩，則教閱有方，講習有素，萬一不虞，用之以禦侮銷患，無難事矣。稽之成周，四時講武，所謂振旅、茇舍、治兵、大閱是已，其制可得而詳歟？秦不師古，盜由廢。炎漢之興，内則有東之之制，外則有都試之名。李唐之世，府兵有一時之講，顯德有習射之較，并州城北、驪山之下，又相有講焉。至于有宋，四時有講武之儀，而郊行大閱之禮，朱明之池、講武之殿，亦相繼有習焉。可各指其實而陳之歟？抑有優劣之可議歟？其亦有合於成周之制否歟？逮于我
translation_en:
…spoken of in general terms, and also those spoken of in interwoven terms; why do they differ from one another? I wish you to set this forth in your essays, so that we may observe your learning in fathoming principles.

Question: Even when the state enjoys a time of peace, military preparedness must not be forgotten. When military preparedness is cultivated, training and reviews follow proper methods, and instruction and practice are maintained habitually; if by chance an unexpected crisis arises, employing these forces to repel aggression and eliminate calamity will be no difficult matter. Examining the era of Completed Zhou, military exercises were conducted in the four seasons—namely what were called "marshaling the troops" (zhenlü), "encamping in the field" (bashe), "drilling the troops" (zhibing), and "the grand review" (dayue). Can the details of these institutions be set forth in full? The Qin did not model itself on antiquity, and banditry arose from this neglect [?]. With the rise of the fiery Han, in the capital there was the institution of the Eastern Garden [? 東之], and in the provinces there was the practice known as the autumn military test at the commandery seat (dushi). In the era of the Li Tang dynasty, the garrison militia (fubing) had its seasonal drills, there were archery competitions at the Xiande Hall, and north of the walls of Bingzhou and at the foot of Mount Li military exercises were also successively held [?]. Coming down to the Song dynasty, there were rituals for military exercises in the four seasons, and the ceremony of the grand review was performed in the suburbs, while at the Zhuming Pool and the Jiangwu Hall practices were likewise conducted one after another. Can you point to the concrete facts of each and set them forth? Or can their relative merits and defects be discussed? And did they accord or not with the institutions of Completed Zhou? Coming down to our…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
朝重熙累洽有安不忘危之慮治兵有律訓
武有方蓋已遠過漢唐宋而與成周匹
休矣孔子曰有文事者必有武備諸士
子素有志於文武者也其為我陳之
punctuated: 朝，重熙累洽，有安不忘危之慮，治兵有律，訓武有方，蓋已遠過漢、唐、宋，而與成周匹休矣。孔子曰：「有文事者，必有武備。」諸士子素有志於文武者也，其為我陳之。
translation_en: …Dynasty, in an era of cumulative splendour and pervasive harmony, there is the foresight of not forgetting danger in times of peace. The governance of the troops follows strict discipline, and military training adheres to proper methods; indeed, it has already far surpassed the Han, Tang, and Song, matching the glory of the glorious Zhou. Confucius said: "Those who have civil affairs must also have military preparations." You scholars have long cherished ambitions in both civil and military matters; set this forth for me.

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
四書
爲仁由己而由人乎哉顔淵曰請問其目子曰
非禮勿視非禮勿聽非禮勿言非禮勿動
王綸

作簡當可式
考試官學正吳　批〔此篇詞理通暢是見講習之學〕
考試官教諭柴　批〔理有定見辭不尚競宜置優選〕
聖人告大賢爲仁當決其機於己答大賢問目當制
===
其欲於己蓋爲仁由己用力之機要也非禮勿視聽
言動用力之條目也欲收克復之功豈外是哉昔聖
人因顔子問仁而告之及此若曰爲仁之道固在於
克己復禮而欲克己復禮果何所用力耶是故仁者
本心之全德非由外鑠我也今焉克己以爲仁則克
己之功我所當任他人庸得而預之仁者吾心之天
理非有待於外也今焉復禮以爲仁則復禮之力己
所當盡若人奚得而干之此其機之在我而無難也
顔子一聞其言則於天理人欲之際已判然矣故不

Four Books

"Does the practice of humanity depend on oneself, or does it depend on others?" Yan Yuan said, "I beg to ask for the specific steps." The Master said, "Do not look at what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not listen to what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not speak what is contrary to ritual propriety; do not make a move that is contrary to ritual propriety."

Wang Lun 
Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Luo comments: [Although the topic itself is plain and straightforward and compositions on it in the examination hall are abundant, only this] piece is concise, fitting, and worthy of serving as a model.
Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Wu comments: [In this essay both the diction and the reasoning flow smoothly, which shows learning grounded in discussion and practice.]
Examiner District Director of Studies Chai comments: [Its reasoning reflects settled insight, and its phrasing does not strive for flashy competition; it ought to be placed among the superior selections.]

The Sage told the great worthy that in practicing humanity one must determine its pivotal trigger within oneself, and in answering the great worthy's question about its specific steps, taught that one must restrain one's desires within oneself. For "the practice of humanity depends on oneself" is the pivotal essential for exerting effort, while "do not look, listen, speak, or move contrary to ritual propriety" are the itemized steps for exerting effort. If one wishes to reap the achievement of overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety, how could it lie outside of this? In the past, when the Sage responded to Master Yan's question about humanity and spoke down to this point, it was as if he said: The Way of practicing humanity surely lies in overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety; yet if one wishes to overcome the self and return to ritual propriety, where indeed should one exert one's effort? Therefore, humanity is the complete virtue of the original mind, not something fused onto me from the outside. Now, in overcoming the self in order to practice humanity, the work of overcoming the self is a responsibility that I myself must bear—how could others take part in it? Humanity is the Heavenly Principle of my own mind, not something dependent on the outside. Now, in returning to ritual propriety in order to practice humanity, the effort of returning to ritual propriety is something that I myself must exhaust—how could others interfere with it? This shows that the pivotal trigger lies within me and presents no difficulty. As soon as Master Yan heard these words, the boundary between Heavenly Principle and human desire was already completely clear to him. Therefore, without…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
復有所疑問而直請其條目焉聖人復告之曰目司
視而耳司聽也視聽非禮則有以害吾仁矣故非禮
之聲色必禁止之而弗視弗聽焉此防其自外入而
動於內者爲何如口主言而身主動也言動非禮則
有以壞吾仁矣故非禮之念慮必消弭之而不言不
動焉此謹其自內出而接於外者又何如內外交進
克復之功盡矣仁之爲道孰有加於此哉抑此章問
答乃聖門傳授心法切要之言也非顏子至明則雖
有克己復禮天下歸仁之告必不能察其幾非顏子
===
至毅則雖有爲仁由己與夫四勿之說必不能致其
決此夫子所以獨告顏子有以夫
不誠無物是故君子誠之爲貴誠者非自成己
而已也所以成物也
李璉
同考試官教諭徐　批〔中庸一題㫖於性理場中作者多泛而不切惟此篇詞理俱到可取〕
考試官教諭桊　批〔理明文暢優於衆作〕
考試官學正吳　批〔此篇得子思論誠之㫖而詞叉〕
punctuated:
復有所疑問，而直請其條目焉。聖人復告之曰：目司視而耳司聽也，視聽非禮，則有以害吾仁矣，故非禮之聲色，必禁止之而弗視弗聽焉，此防其自外入而動於內者爲何如？口主言而身主動也，言動非禮，則有以壞吾仁矣，故非禮之念慮，必消弭之而不言不動焉，此謹其自內出而接於外者又何如？內外交進，克復之功盡矣。仁之爲道，孰有加於此哉？抑此章問答，乃聖門傳授心法切要之言也。非顏子至明，則雖有「克己復禮，天下歸仁」之告，必不能察其幾；非顏子至毅，則雖有「爲仁由己」與夫「四勿」之說，必不能致其決。此夫子所以獨告顏子，有以夫！
「不誠無物。是故君子誠之爲貴。誠者，非自成己而已也，所以成物也。」
李璉
同考試官教諭徐　批〔《中庸》一題，㫖於性理，場中作者多泛而不切，惟此篇詞理俱到，可取。〕
考試官教諭桊　批〔理明文暢，優於衆作。〕
考試官學正吳　批〔此篇得子思論誠之㫖，而詞叉〕
translation_en:
…again have any doubts or questions, and directly asked for the specific items of practice. The Sage again told him: "The eyes govern seeing and the ears govern hearing. If seeing and hearing are contrary to ritual propriety, they will harm one's benevolence. Therefore, sights and sounds that are contrary to ritual propriety must be prohibited so that one neither looks at nor listens to them. How thorough is this in guarding against what enters from the outside to stir the inside! The mouth presides over speech and the body presides over action. If speech and action are contrary to ritual propriety, they will ruin one's benevolence. Therefore, thoughts and intentions that are contrary to ritual propriety must be dispelled so that one neither speaks nor acts upon them. And how careful is this in watching over what issues from the inside to engage with the outside!" Advancing both internally and externally, the work of overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety is exhausted. As for the Way of benevolence, what could be added to this? Moreover, the questions and answers in this chapter are the essential words by which the Sage's school transmitted the method of the mind-and-heart. Had Master Yan (Yanzi 顏子) not been supremely perspicacious, then even with the teaching of "overcoming the self and returning to ritual propriety, so that all under heaven will ascribe benevolence to one," he certainly could not have discerned its subtle incipient stirrings. Had Master Yan not been supremely resolute, then even with the doctrines that "practicing benevolence depends on oneself" and the "Four Prohibitions," he certainly could not have achieved such decisiveness. That the Master imparted this solely to Master Yan was indeed for good reason!

"Without sincerity there would be nothing. Therefore the noble man regards attaining sincerity as precious. Sincerity is not merely the completion of oneself; it is that by which one completes all things."

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
不冗絕吳他作
誠不可無人當實其心誠爲已有自然及於物盖人
心不實則無其物不可不實之也能實其心而自成
焉豈不有以及於物哉且夫誠者真實無妄之謂誠
在於人則爲實心人心一有不實則雖有所爲亦如
無有如事親不誠於孝則孝之一物無有也事兄不
誠於弟則弟之一物無有也是以君子知不誠則無
是物必以誠之爲貴如事親者當實其孝於已焉知
不實則無是事如事兄者當實其弟於已焉盖人之
===
心能無不實乃爲有以自成而道之在我者亦無不
行矣然誠雖所以成已豈徒自成而已哉成不獨成
而自有以成乎物也抑豈但成已而已哉立不獨立
而自有以立乎彼也如孝能自成孝不爲已有而彼
亦得以成其孝焉如弟能自成弟不爲已私而彼亦
得以成其弟焉盖誠能成已則自然及物而道亦行
於彼矣誠之爲道豈不盡乎抑中庸是章言人道而
以誠論之誠一也在天爲實理在人爲實心如上文
所謂誠者自成誠者物之終始此以實理言也所謂
punctuated:
〔不冗，絕吳他作。〕
誠不可無，人當實其心；誠爲已有，自然及於物。盖人心不實，則無其物，不可不實之也。能實其心而自成焉，豈不有以及於物哉？且夫誠者，真實無妄之謂。誠在於人，則爲實心。人心一有不實，則雖有所爲，亦如無有。如事親不誠於孝，則孝之一物無有也；事兄不誠於弟，則弟之一物無有也。是以君子知不誠則無是物，必以誠之爲貴，如事親者當實其孝於已焉；知不實則無是事，如事兄者當實其弟於已焉。盖人之心能無不實，乃爲有以自成，而道之在我者亦無不行矣。然誠雖所以成已，豈徒自成而已哉？成不獨成，而自有以成乎物也；抑豈但成已而已哉？立不獨立，而自有以立乎彼也。如孝能自成，孝不爲已有，而彼亦得以成其孝焉；如弟能自成，弟不爲已私，而彼亦得以成其弟焉。盖誠能成已，則自然及物，而道亦行於彼矣。誠之爲道，豈不盡乎？抑《中庸》是章言人道而以誠論之。誠一也，在天爲實理，在人爲實心。如上文所謂「誠者自成」、「誠者物之終始」，此以實理言也；所謂
translation_en:
…〔is not verbose, utterly different [?] from the other compositions.〕

Sincerity cannot be lacking, so a person ought to make his mind real; when sincerity becomes one's own possession, it naturally extends to other things. For if the human mind is not real, then the thing itself ceases to exist, so one cannot fail to make it real. If one is able to make one's mind real and thereby complete oneself, how could it not also extend to other things?

Now, sincerity means being genuinely real and free from falsehood. As it exists in a person, sincerity is a real mind. Once there is any lack of reality in the human mind, even if one engages in some action, it is as though nothing were there at all. For instance, if in serving one's parents one is not sincere in filial piety, then that thing which is filial piety does not exist; if in serving one's elder brother one is not sincere in fraternal respect, then that thing which is fraternal respect does not exist. Therefore, because the superior man knows that without sincerity there is no such thing, he necessarily values the attainment of sincerity—just as one who serves his parents ought to make filial piety real within himself; and because he knows that without reality there is no such deed, one who serves his elder brother ought to make fraternal respect real within himself.

For when a person's mind can be entirely free from unreality, he thereby has the means to complete himself, and the Way as it resides in him will also be practiced without fail. Yet although sincerity is the means by which one completes oneself, how could it merely be a matter of completing oneself and nothing more? In completing oneself, one does not complete oneself alone, but naturally has the means to complete other things as well. And how could it merely be a matter of completing oneself? In establishing oneself, one does not establish oneself alone, but naturally has the means to establish others as well. For instance, if in filial piety one is able to complete oneself, filial piety does not remain one's own possession alone, and others are also enabled to complete their filial piety; if in fraternal respect one is able to complete oneself, fraternal respect does not remain one's private possession alone, and others are also enabled to complete their fraternal respect. For when sincerity is able to complete the self, it naturally extends to other things, and the Way is practiced among others as well. Is not the Way of sincerity thus exhausted?

Furthermore, this chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) speaks of the Way of man and discusses it in terms of sincerity. Sincerity is one: in Heaven it is real principle, and in man it is a real mind. Thus, when the preceding text says "Sincerity is self-completion" and "Sincerity is the beginning and end of things," this is spoken of in terms of real principle; whereas when it says…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
而道自道與此節言誠此以實心言也然在天本無
不實之理而在人或有不實之心學者果能加誠之
之功則心無不實而在天者在我矣尚其勉之
詩云雨我公田遂及我私惟助為有公田由此
觀之雖周亦助也設為庠序學校以教之庠
者養也校者教也序者射也夏曰校殷曰序
周曰庠學則三代共之皆所以明人倫也
朱昂

考試官學正吳　批〔說理明而文足以發之作手也〕
===
大賢之告滕君也既釋詩以見前代養民之制復詳
言以見前代教民之制蓋助法所以養民而庠序學
校所以教民也大賢之於滕君得不兼舉以為告哉
昔孟子勸文公之行助法故引大田之詩而謂夫雨我
公田遂及我私蓋公田為君子之養在所當先故民人
punctuated:
而道自道，與此節言「誠」，此以實心言也。然在天本無不實之理，而在人或有不實之心。學者果能加誠之之功，則心無不實，而在天者在我矣，尚其勉之。

《詩》云：「雨我公田，遂及我私。」惟助為有公田。由此觀之，雖周亦助也。設為庠、序、學、校以教之：庠者，養也；校者，教也；序者，射也。夏曰校，殷曰序，周曰庠；學則三代共之，皆所以明人倫也。

朱昂
同考試官訓導夏　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
同考試官訓導吳　批〔□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
考試官教諭樂　批〔據理作詞，發明孟子之□□□。〕
考試官學正吳　批〔說理明而文足以發之，作手也。〕

大賢之告滕君也，既釋《詩》以見前代養民之制，復詳言以見前代教民之制。蓋助法所以養民，而庠、序、學、校所以教民也。大賢之於滕君，得不兼舉以為告哉？昔孟子勸文公之行助法，故引《大田》之詩，而謂夫「雨我公田，遂及我私」。蓋公田為君子之養，在所當先，故民人
translation_en:
… "and the Way is that which one must pursue by oneself," along with the discussion of "sincerity" in this section—these are spoken of in terms of a true heart-and-mind. Yet while in Heaven there is fundamentally no principle that is not real, in human beings there may sometimes be a heart-and-mind that is not true. If scholars can truly apply the effort of making it sincere, then there will be nothing untrue in the heart-and-mind, and what is in Heaven will be within oneself. May they strive at this!

The Book of Odes (Shijing) says: "May it rain on our public fields, and then reach our private ones." Only under the mutual-aid (zhu) system are there public fields. Viewed from this, even the Zhou also used the mutual-aid system. Establish xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools to instruct them: xiang means to nourish; xiao means to instruct; xu means archery. The Xia called them xiao, the Yin called them xu, and the Zhou called them xiang; as for xue, the Three Dynasties shared the name. All of them are means by which to clarify human moral relations.

Zhu Ang

When the Great Worthy advised the ruler of Teng, he first explained the Book of Odes to show the former dynasties' system for nourishing the people, and then spoke in detail to show the former dynasties' system for instructing the people. For the mutual-aid method is that by which the people are nourished, while the xiang, xu, xue, and xiao schools are that by which the people are instructed. In addressing the ruler of Teng, how could the Great Worthy not cite both in order to advise him? In the past, Mencius urged Duke Wen to practice the mutual-aid method, and therefore quoted the ode "Large Fields" (Datian), saying: "May it rain on our public fields, and then reach our private ones." This is because the public fields provide nourishment for the superior men and ought to be put first; therefore the common people…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
願天之雨必先于是焉私田爲小人之養在所當後
故農人欲雨之降遂及于我焉是惟助法之行而有
此公田之制然今之助法不行久矣由是詩而觀之
則不惟見商之用助而周亦用乎助焉以此詩而驗
之則不惟見殷之行此而周亦行乎此焉前代養民
之制如此君其可不行乎然養民固有以遂其生非
敎民則無以復其性故又告以設爲庠序以敎之立
爲學校以訓之蓋庠以養老爲義校以敎民爲義序
以習射爲義鄉學之義固不同也在夏而曰校在殷
===
而曰序在周而曰庠鄉學之名亦有異也以至國學
之名則三代有以共之焉然夏商與周學有大小而
明倫之道無大小之殊庠序學校制有彼此而敎與
之意無彼此之間前代敎民之制如此君其可不盡
乎吁助法行而民有所養學校立而民有所敎孟子
欲滕君之行仁政豈外是哉抑戰國之時王道不明
井田學校不行久矣孟子既告滕君以此而他日又
以經界示畢戰雖當制度已廢之餘能因略以致詳
推舊而爲新不屑屑於既往之迹而能合乎先王之
punctuated:
願天之雨，必先于是焉；私田爲小人之養，在所當後，故農人欲雨之降，遂及于我焉。是惟助法之行，而有此公田之制。然今之助法不行久矣。由是詩而觀之，則不惟見商之用助，而周亦用乎助焉；以此詩而驗之，則不惟見殷之行此，而周亦行乎此焉。前代養民之制如此，君其可不行乎？

然養民固有以遂其生，非敎民則無以復其性。故又告以設爲庠、序以敎之，立爲學、校以訓之。蓋庠以養老爲義，校以敎民爲義，序以習射爲義，鄉學之義固不同也；在夏而曰校，在殷而曰序，在周而曰庠，鄉學之名亦有異也；以至國學之名，則三代有以共之焉。然夏、商與周，學有大小，而明倫之道無大小之殊；庠、序、學、校，制有彼此，而敎與之意無彼此之間。前代敎民之制如此，君其可不盡乎？

吁！助法行而民有所養，學校立而民有所敎，孟子欲滕君之行仁政，豈外是哉！抑戰國之時，王道不明，井田、學校不行久矣。孟子既告滕君以此，而他日又以經界示畢戰。雖當制度已廢之餘，能因略以致詳，推舊而爲新，不屑屑於既往之迹，而能合乎先王之
translation_en:
…wish that Heaven's rain must fall upon it first. The private fields provide nourishment for the commoners and properly come after; therefore the farmers desire that when the rain descends, it should then reach our own fields. It is only through the practice of the mutual-aid system (zhu) that this institution of the public field exists. Yet in the present day, the mutual-aid system has long cease to be practiced. Viewed through this ode, however, one sees not only that the Shang used the mutual-aid system, but that the Zhou used it as well; verified by this ode, one sees not only that the Yin practiced this, but that the Zhou practiced it as well. Such was the system of nourishing the people in former dynasties—how could my lord not put it into practice?

Yet while nourishing the people indeed enables them to fulfill their livelihood, without educating the people there is no way to restore their innate nature. Therefore, he further advised establishing xiang and xu to teach them, and setting up xue and xiao to instruct them. Now, xiang means "nourishing the aged," xiao means "educating the people," and xu means "practicing archery"—the meanings of these district schools are indeed different. In the Xia it was called xiao, in the Yin it was called xu, and in the Zhou it was called xiang—the names of these district schools also varied. As for the name of the state academy (xue), the Three Dynasties shared it in common. Nevertheless, across the Xia, Shang, and Zhou, although schools were either great or small, the Way of clarifying human relationships had no distinction between great and small; among the xiang, xu, xue, and xiao, although the institutions differed from one another, the intention of imparting education had no gap between one and another. Such was the system of educating the people in former dynasties—how could my lord not carry it out to the utmost?

Alas! When the mutual-aid system is practiced, the people have the means to be nourished; when schools are established, the people have the means to be educated. In desiring the ruler of Teng to practice benevolent governance, how could Mencius have looked beyond these? Moreover, during the Warring States period, the Kingly Way was obscured, and the well-field system and schools had long been out of practice. Having advised the ruler of Teng with these words, Mencius on another day further explained the division of field boundaries to Bi Zhan. Even after the institutions had already fallen into ruin, he was able to proceed from the rough outline to arrive at the details, extending the old to make it new; without being bogged down in the traces of the past, he was able to conform to the former kings'…

text:
意者真可謂命世亞聖之才矣
易
利有攸往中正有慶
白震

聖人釋卦辭宜往之占必即卦體宜往之善蓋慶益
===
之時往无不利所以然者得非由二五之中正有慶
乎宜聖人彖傳發揮以示人也且夫益之爲卦合震
巽而成體文王繫辭以利有攸往而著其占吾夫子
彖傳從而釋之謂夫當損上益下之時民心已說而
無疆吾道既大而且光不有攸往則已往則順理而
行自與吉會无一而不利焉不有攸行則已行則惠
迪之吉勿問可知无一而不宜焉所以然者蓋以卦
體二五之中正有慶故爾九五居上體之中而當陽
位之正六二居下體之中而當陰位之正五之應二
punctuated:
意者，真可謂命世亞聖之才矣。

《易》
「利有攸往，中正有慶。」
白震

聖人釋卦辭宜往之占，必即卦體宜往之善。蓋慶益之時，往无不利。所以然者，得非由二五之中正有慶乎？宜聖人《彖傳》發揮以示人也。且夫益之爲卦，合震、巽而成體。文王繫辭以「利有攸往」而著其占，吾夫子《彖傳》從而釋之。謂夫當損上益下之時，民心已說而無疆，吾道既大而且光。不有攸往則已，往則順理而行，自與吉會，无一而不利焉；不有攸行則已，行則惠迪之吉，勿問可知，无一而不宜焉。所以然者，蓋以卦體二五之中正有慶故爾。九五居上體之中，而當陽位之正；六二居下體之中，而當陰位之正。五之應二…
translation_en:
… the intentions [of the former kings], he can truly be called a talent of a generation and a Second Sage!

Book of Changes (Yi)
"It is favorable to have somewhere to go: central and correct, there is celebration."
Bai Zhen 白震
Associate Examiner, Assistant Instructor Zhou 周 comments: [He brings out the meaning of the hexagram structure and the Judgment words with intimacy, conciseness, and aptness. Compared to those who chase after empty words and [miss?] the classical meaning, this is vastly different; he deserves to be placed among the selected.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wu 吳 comments: [His elucidation of the hexagram statement deeply accords with the Original Meaning (Benyi).]
Examiner, County Director of Studies Chai 柴 comments: [His phrasing is smooth and the purport clear; he is evidently one who excels in the study of the Changes.]

When the Sage explains the prognostication in the hexagram statement that it is fitting to go forth, he necessarily grounds it in the excellence of the hexagram's structure that makes going forth fitting. For in a time of celebratory increase, wherever one goes there is nothing unfavorable. That it is so—is it not because the second and fifth lines are central and correct, and thus bring celebration? Fittingly did the Sage elaborate upon this in the Commentary on the Judgment (Tuanzhuan) to show it to mankind.

Moreover, as a hexagram, Increase (Yi 益) combines the trigrams Zhen 震 and Xun 巽 to form its structure. King Wen appended the words "It is favorable to have somewhere to go" to make manifest its prognostication, and our Master in the Commentary on the Judgment followed by explaining it. He meant that at a time of diminishing the above to increase the below, the minds of the people are already pleased without limit, and our Way is both great and glorious. If one does not have somewhere to go, then nothing more need be said; but if one goes, one acts in accordance with principle and naturally meets with good fortune, there being nothing at all that is not favorable. If one does not set out to act, then nothing more need be said; but if one acts, the good fortune of following the right path can be known without even asking, there being nothing at all that is not fitting. The reason it is so is simply because in the hexagram's structure, lines two and five are central and correct, and therefore bring celebration. The Nine in the Fifth resides in the center of the upper trigram and occupies the correct yang position; the Six in the Second resides in the center of the lower trigram and occupies the correct yin position. The fifth's correspondence with the second…

title: 成化元年山東鄉試錄
text:
也以此中正之道二之應五也亦此中正之德二五
皆得中正是以明良相逢而君臣得以際亨嘉之慶
德澤流行而天下有以受康寧之福卦辭利有攸往
寧不本於此哉嘗觀易之諸卦言利從不言利涉益
彖何以兼而有之蓋益以益下為本本固則無所不
利此所以行則利往濟則利涉也大傳曰益以興利
詎不信夫
===
歸奇於扐以象閏五歲再閏故再扐而後掛乾
之策二百一十有六坤之策百四十有四凡
三百有六十當期之日
同考試官訓導周　批〔推合傳註成文殊勝他作驥〕〔出而馬群空顧不信歟〕
敖山
考試官教諭棠　批〔蓍法一題衆所寡者惟此作得之〕
考試官學正呉　批〔能識出理數之旨士為佳作〕
聖人即歸餘蓍數以象月之閏合乾坤蓍數以象歲
之周蓋蓍策之數與天地之數無往而不合也然皆
出於理勢之自然豈人之智力能損益哉且夫揲蓍
punctuated:
也，以此中正之道；二之應五也，亦此中正之德。二五皆得中正，是以明良相逢，而君臣得以際亨嘉之慶；德澤流行，而天下有以受康寧之福。卦辭「利有攸往」，寧不本於此哉？嘗觀《易》之諸卦，言利從不言利涉，益《彖》何以兼而有之？蓋益以益下為本，本固則無所不利，此所以行則利往、濟則利涉也。《大傳》曰：「益以興利。」詎不信夫！

「歸奇於扐以象閏，五歲再閏，故再扐而後掛。乾之策二百一十有六，坤之策百四十有四，凡三百有六十，當期之日。」
同考試官訓導周　批：〔推合傳註成文，殊勝他作。驥〕〔出而馬群空，顧不信歟？〕
敖山
